title: Lock down the exposed Supabase schema behind the BFF
description: The browser uses Supabase directly only for Auth and profile-media Storage, but public-schema table grants plus permissive RLS expose internal rows through PostgREST. Anonymous callers can read profile ids and timestamps, the full follow graph, handle history, all likes and reposts, and public or unlisted post and reply rows; this bypasses sanitized server views and indirect visibility revocation. Authenticated callers can also directly mutate their profile handle and archive metadata, bypassing API invariants. Revoke unnecessary anon and authenticated table access or replace it with narrowly safe views or RPCs while retaining required Storage policies.
acceptance_criteria: Anon and authenticated callers cannot query internal UUIDs or interaction rows outside intended public contracts; a target made private cannot remain discoverable through likes, reposts, or replies via PostgREST; hidden follow lists are not readable directly; profile handles and archive metadata cannot be mutated outside the BFF; pgTAP tests enumerate required grants and prove denied direct access; application routes still work.

title: Isolate and bound the custom feed cache
description: The process cache and in-flight map in feeds.ts are keyed only by sourceId. Two visitors can submit different custom feed URLs with the same local id and receive each others cached feed, and unlimited distinct custom ids grow the maps for the life of an instance. Cache identity must include immutable feed identity and storage must be bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Different custom URLs sharing an id never share cached or in-flight content; catalog behavior is unchanged; cache entries have an explicit size/eviction policy; stale revalidation cannot write into the wrong identity; tests reproduce the cross-request collision and verify eviction.
close_reason: Cache identity now includes feed URL and both process-local stores use bounded LRU eviction; regression tests added.

title: Close DNS-rebinding and IPv6 gaps in outbound fetch protection
description: safeFeedFetch and safeContentFetch resolve a hostname to validate it, then fetch the hostname through a separate DNS resolution. An attacker-controlled hostname can change answers between those steps and reach private services. IPv4-mapped and alternate-form IPv6 checks are also incomplete. Both the public source preview and authenticated content capture use this boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The connection is constrained to a validated public address or otherwise cannot re-resolve to a private target; redirects are revalidated; normalized IPv4, IPv6, IPv4-mapped IPv6, loopback, link-local, private, multicast, documentation, and cloud-metadata ranges are covered; DNS rebinding tests fail against the old implementation and pass against the fix; feed preview and content capture share the hardened primitive.
close_reason: Pinned outbound HTTPS connections to validated DNS answers, unified feed/content URL validation, and added IPv6/DNS regression coverage.

title: Make handle changes atomic and database-enforced
description: The three-per-year rate check runs in TypeScript before change_handle and is raceable. SupabaseProfileStore.save calls change_handle in one request, then performs a separate upsert that includes handle, creating a second race and partial-success window. Direct profile UPDATE currently bypasses the whole mechanism. Move rate enforcement and row locking into the database transaction, prevent ordinary profile updates from changing handle, and keep non-handle profile saving coherent after a rename.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent rename attempts cannot exceed the rolling limit, lose a history edge, or overwrite a later handle; a failed profile field save has defined behavior after rename; no direct client UPDATE can bypass quarantine or rate limits; first profile creation remains supported; pgTAP and API tests cover concurrency/integrity and limit boundaries.
close_reason: Profile saves now use one locked DB transaction for handle history, quarantine, rolling rate limit, and field updates; direct handle changes are guarded.

title: Migration A: four-value visibility type swap + publish_collection rebuild
description:
Replace the two-value collection_publication_visibility enum with a four-value public.visibility type.

This CANNOT be an ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE. Postgres will not let a value added in a transaction be used in that same transaction, and Supabase runs each migration file in one transaction. So it is a new type plus a column swap with USING - which drags publish_collection() with it, because that function signature names the old type.

Highest-blast-radius migration in the plan. A partial application leaves publishing broken for every user. Rehearse against a local supabase db reset before it goes anywhere near a deployed database.
design:
Ordered steps, one transaction, one file:
1. create type public.visibility as enum ("private", "followers", "unlisted", "public");   -- order matters: least to most visible
2. alter table public.collection_publications add column visibility_new public.visibility;
3. update ... set visibility_new = visibility::text::public.visibility;   -- 1:1 map, per the resolved decision. unlisted stays unlisted, public stays public. No existing row becomes more visible.
4. alter column visibility_new set not null, set default "unlisted";
5. drop the two select policies that reference the old column, drop the old column, rename visibility_new to visibility.
6. Recreate collection_publications_live_idx (dropping the old column drops the index).
7. drop function public.publish_collection(uuid, uuid, text, text, public.collection_publication_visibility, text, text, text, text, jsonb);  -- the FULL old signature
8. create or replace the function with p_visibility public.visibility, otherwise unchanged.
9. Re-apply the revoke from public, anon, authenticated and the grant execute to service_role FOR THE NEW SIGNATURE. A grant does not follow a signature change.
10. Recreate the two select policies against the new column.
11. drop type public.collection_publication_visibility;   -- last

Then update the TypeScript: PublicationVisibility in src/lib/collectionPublication.ts widens to four values, and parsePublicationSnapshot / parsePublishRequest (which currently hard-code the string comparison against unlisted and public) accept all four.

Discovery listings keep filtering to visibility = "public" at the query level, per the existing comment in the collection_publications migration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Migration applies cleanly against a fresh supabase db reset and against a database seeded with existing publications.
- Every pre-existing row keeps its exact prior visibility. Nothing becomes more visible.
- publish_collection works end to end after the migration, for both a first publish and a republish.
- The revoke/grant pair is correct for the new signature: service_role can execute, anon and authenticated cannot.
- Both select policies exist and reference the new column.
- The old type no longer exists.
- pgTAP asserts the policy set and the grant set before and after.
notes:
DONE 2026-09-06. Files: supabase/migrations/20260906140000_visibility_type_swap.sql; supabase/tests/visibility_type_swap.test.sql (plan 23); collectionPublication.ts (4-value type + isPublicationVisibility guard, both parse fns); +2 unit tests; old-type casts in collection_publications.test.sql / profile_surface.test.sql swapped to public.visibility.

DEVIATION FROM DESIGN: the plan said 'two select policies' reference the column; there are THREE. The third is collection_follows.'followers manage their own follows' (FOR ALL) whose WITH CHECK subquery reads collection_publications.visibility. Migration drops+recreates all three, verbatim from their origin migrations.

title: Preview: fix embedCompatibility trigger (per-article + keep modal on unknown)
description:
The iframe-vs-fallback trigger is unreliable:
1. embedCompatibility is computed once per feed from articles[0].url (feeds.server.ts:195) via a HEAD request. Many origins omit X-Frame-Options/CSP on HEAD or vary it per path, so the whole feed inherits a wrong/ verdict for 24h.
2. NewsApp.openStory treats compatibility === 'unknown' as 'skip the modal, just window.open' - so for every feed where detection failed the reader never sees a preview or a card at all.

Scope:
- Compute compatibility per-article, not per-feed. Prefer reusing response headers already fetched elsewhere (fetchSafeContent in the preview path returns responseHeaders) rather than a second network call; where a standalone check is still needed use GET, not HEAD, and read only headers.
- In openStory, stop bypassing the modal on 'unknown'. 'unknown' -> open the modal in a degraded mode that offers the reader view / metadata card (same as 'blocked') plus a clear 'Open original'. Only articlePreviewMode === 'external' bypasses.
- Keep the 24h TTL for confirmed allowed/blocked; keep the short TTL for unknown so a transient failure re-checks soon.
- Update compatibilityFromHeaders tests + interaction.test.tsx for the new 'unknown shows modal' behavior.
acceptance_criteria: compatibility reflects the actual article URL's headers, not just articles[0]; 'unknown' opens the preview modal with the card/reader-view fallback instead of silently opening external; no extra HEAD/GET round-trip when headers are already available from fetchSafeContent; tests updated for per-article detection and the unknown-shows-modal path.
notes: Shell note: earlier create dropped one word to a backtick glitch. The HEAD verdict issue is: the whole feed inherits a wrong or unknown verdict for 24h.
close_reason: Per-article embed detection: new /api/embed-compatibility route probes the exact article URL (GET, headers-only via fetchValidatedHttps maxBytes:0), cache keyed by URL not feed. openStory only bypasses the modal for articlePreviewMode==='external'; 'unknown' opens the modal with the static fallback. createArticlePreview reconciles the verdict from fetchSafeContent headers (no extra round-trip). Removed the per-feed articles[0] HEAD probe. Tests: 497 unit + 73 UI green, lint + tsc + build clean.

title: Preview: publisher metadata card fallback for blocked embeds
description: Replace the non-functional screenshot path (for compatibility === 'blocked') with a server-extracted metadata card: og:image / twitter:image, og:title (fallback ), og:description (fallback meta description), domain, favicon. Source all of it from the HTML that fetchSafeContent already retrieves in createArticlePreview - no browser, no new infra, works in production immediately. Scope: - New pure module (e.g. src/lib/articleMetadata.ts) that parses OG/Twitter/standard meta + favicon href from an HTML string + base URL. Unit-tested via *.test.mjs (keep it importable - no 'import server-only', per server-only-vs-node-test memory). - Wire createArticlePreview / a new lightweight endpoint to return the card data as JSON (not PNG). Keep the robots + opt-out + pageDisallowsPreview + pageAppearsAccessRestricted gates in front of it. - StaticSourcePreview in src/components/ArticlePreview.tsx renders the card (image with onError fallback to favicon+domain, title, description, 'Read at {host}'). - Resolve og:image through validatedHttpsUrl and proxy/allowlist it the same way other outbound assets are handled; never hotlink an arbitrary remote URL into an <img> without the CSP/SSRF story. Decide: proxy bytes through a bounded route vs. add to img-src. Document the choice. - Favicon: prefer <link rel=icon>, fall back to /favicon.ico, same SSRF rules.
acceptance_criteria: blocked-embed articles show a metadata card in production; card degrades to favicon+domain+title when og:image missing/failing; policy gates (robots, opt-out, page directives, paywall heuristic) still enforced; og:image/favicon fetched only through validatedHttpsUrl; unit tests cover OG/Twitter/standard/missing-tag extraction and favicon resolution; no Playwright import on this path.
close_reason: Metadata card fallback shipped. New pure src/lib/articleMetadata.ts (extractArticleCard: og/twitter/standard meta + favicon, https-only, relative-resolved; 6 unit tests). createArticleCard() in articlePreview.server.ts reuses fetchSafeContent HTML behind the same gates (opt-out/robots/pageDisallowsPreview/pageAppearsAccessRestricted), 1h cache. New routes: /api/article-preview/card (JSON) and /api/article-preview/image (bounded same-origin proxy: validatedHttpsUrl + 2MB cap + image/* non-SVG check + nosniff + CSP default-src none). StaticSourcePreview rewritten: loading -> card (image w/ onError to favicon+domain, title, description) -> unavailable message. Decision documented in PRD 6.1.2: proxy bytes, not img-src allowlist (no per-publisher CSP surface, no IP/referer leak). Follow-up bareaga_web-cto filed for HMAC-signing the proxy URLs. 503 unit + 75 UI green, lint+tsc+build clean.

title: [EPIC] Rework source preview for non-embeddable pages
description:
The static source preview shown when a publisher blocks iframe embedding does not work in production. renderOfflineScreenshot() in src/lib/articlePreview.server.ts does await import('playwright') + chromium.launch(), but 'playwright' is only a transitive devDependency and no Chromium binary ships to Vercel, so every call throws, /api/article-preview returns 404, and the reader sees 'Preview unavailable'. Even locally the render is low fidelity (JS disabled, 24-asset cap, fixed 1200x630 top clip catching nav/cookie banners). The embedCompatibility trigger is also weak: computed once per feed from articles[0] via HEAD, and 'unknown' currently bypasses the modal entirely.

This epic replaces the per-request headless screenshot with a layered, cheapest-first fallback: (1) publisher metadata card, (2) in-Coeus reader view from server-side content extraction, (3) hosted screenshot API only if a literal visual is ever required. Keep articlePreviewPolicy.ts (robots parser, page directives, opt-out), safeContentFetch/safeOutboundFetch hardening, the /source-preview-opt-out page, and PRD 6.1.2 policy - all rendering-strategy-agnostic.
design: Layered fallback, cheapest first: metadata card (no new infra) -> reader view (content extraction, evaluate Readability+linkedom vs defuddle on parallel spike branches) -> hosted screenshot API (Microlink/ScreenshotOne) only if required. Retire the in-route Playwright path. All paths stay behind articlePreviewPolicy + safeContentFetch.
close_reason: Layered fallback is on main (4fb9bcc): metadata card (0bs.1), per-article embed + unknown-opens-modal (0bs.2), Defuddle reader view with Blob cache (0bs.3-5), Playwright screenshot path removed (0bs.6), indexing signals (0bs.7-8). Follow-up HMAC image-proxy signing remains as bareaga_web-cto (P3), not this epic.

title: profile-media bucket + avatar/cover URL: no host pin, no MIME/size limit (F-24 + F-25)
description: Two halves of the same media-bucket weakness; one PR. F-25: profiles CHECK is avatar_url ~ '^https?://[^/]+/storage/v1/object/public/profile-media/' — [^/]+ is ANY host, http allowed, no / prefix required. validateProfileInput.normalizeBucketUrl only trims. handleSaveProfile never checks the URL came from the upload route. So PUT /api/account/profile can set avatarUrl='https://evil.example/storage/v1/object/public/profile-media/x.svg' -> profile page renders at attacker host (CSP img-src https: allows it). Content injection + visitor-IP logging on every profile view. F-24: storage.buckets row for profile-media has public=true but NO file_size_limit and NO allowed_mime_types. authenticated insert/update/delete policies scope to / prefix only. A signed-in browser with the publishable key can POST arbitrary bytes (HTML/SVG/JS) to Storage REST under a public *.supabase.co URL, bypassing profileUpload.ts magic-byte + size validation.
design: F-25: pin in BOTH the CHECK and validateProfileInput — host must equal NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL origin, scheme https, path prefix profile-media/<uid>/. Tighten CSP img-src from 'https:' to the Supabase project origin + 'self' data: blob:. F-24: ALTER the bucket to set allowed_mime_types (png/jpeg/webp) + file_size_limit (5MB). Drop the client insert/update policies; make the media route the only writer (service role), OR issue signed upload URLs after validateUpload passes. Keep public read.
acceptance_criteria: Migration + validator change. pgTAP: a doctored avatar_url (foreign host, http, wrong uid prefix) fails the CHECK. Unit: validateProfileInput rejects the same. Storage REST insert of text/html to <uid>/ is refused by the bucket MIME limit (or by removing the client policy). Existing profileUpload + profileEditor tests green. CSP smoke (scripts/security-headers-smoke) updated.
notes: DECISION (2026-09-09, user): F-24 = BFF-only. DROP the authenticated insert/update storage policies on profile-media entirely; all avatar/cover writes go through /api/account/profile/media (handleUploadProfileMedia, already validates magic bytes + size + writes under <uid>/). Keep the delete policy OR move delete to BFF too. Also set allowed_mime_types (image/png,image/jpeg,image/webp) + file_size_limit (5242880) on the bucket as belt-and-braces. Before dropping policies: grep for any client-side supabase.storage.from('profile-media') write — expected none (browser client is Auth + read only per lock_down_public_tables intent). Keep 'anyone reads profile media' select policy.
close_reason: F-24+F-25 fixed on working tree (not committed): migration 20260909140000_profile_media_lockdown.sql drops client insert/update storage policies (BFF-only; media route now uses admin client), sets allowed_mime_types+file_size_limit on the bucket, tightens avatar/cover CHECK to ^https://.../profile-media/<uuid>/. normalizeBucketUrl (exported) host-pins to NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL + uuid prefix and validateProfileInput now errors on a non-bucket URL. CSP img-src narrowed from https: to self data: blob: + supabase origin. profile_surface.test.sql extended (27 assertions). supabase test db PASS (300); 480 unit + 66 UI green.

title: /api/test/session not fail-closed for prod; POST accepts any email (F-26)
description: testLoginEnabled() = E2E_TEST_LOGIN==='1' && VERCEL_ENV!=='production'. title: safeNext open redirect via /\evil.com — helper copied 3x (F-19)
description: safeNext allows any string starting with / and not //. '/\evil.com' passes both checks; WHATWG resolves /\ to an authority, so new URL('/\evil.com','https://app').href => 'https://evil.com/'. src/app/auth/callback/route.ts then Response.redirect(new URL(next,url),302) immediately after exchangeCodeForSession sets session cookies. acceptance_criteria: Unit test covers /\evil.com, //evil.com, /\/evil.com, https://evil.com, /%2f%2fevil.com, plain '/archive?x=1' (kept), '' and null (fallback). All 3 call sites use the shared primitive. tsc + lint + npm test green.
close_reason: Added src/lib/safeRedirect.ts (safeInternalPath primitive: rejects backslash/whitespace/control chars, then confirms same-origin via new URL origin check) + safeRedirect.test.mjs (5 tests incl the /\evil.com vector). title: Source preview bypasses SSRF DNS pinning (F-23)
description: previewFeedUrl -> resolveFeedUrl(rawUrl) with no fetcher arg. resolveFeedUrl's signature defaults fetcher = fetch (feedDiscovery.server.ts:47), so fetchFeedText takes the fetcher(url,init) branch and does an UNPINNED fetch after validatedHttpsUrl already resolved+checked the address. That reopens the DNS-rebinding window the fixedAddressLookup pin exists to close. Unauthenticated POST /api/sources/preview; rate limit is process-local only. Catalog feeds.server.ts and content capture pass no fetcher and stay pinned.
design: Change resolveFeedUrl signature to 'fetcher: typeof fetch | undefined = undefined' (match fetchFeedText / fetchSafeContent) and drop '= fetch'. Passing undefined at the call site is NOT enough — it re-triggers the default.
acceptance_criteria: resolveFeedUrl with no fetcher arg routes through fetchValidatedHttps (pinned). Existing injected-fetcher tests still pass. New test asserts previewFeedUrl uses the pinned path (e.g. a spy resolve/lookup is consulted and global fetch is not called).
close_reason: Changed resolveFeedUrl fetcher default from global fetch to undefined so previewFeedUrl routes through the DNS-pinned fetchValidatedHttps path. Added regression test 'with no fetcher, never calls global fetch'. tsc + lint + 473 unit tests green.

title: Feed fetch broken: custom DNS lookup hook doesn't support {all:true} (Node autoSelectFamily)
description: fetchValidatedHttps in safeOutboundFetch.server.ts passes a lookup hook that always calls callback(null, address, family). Node's autoSelectFamily (default true, Node 20+) invokes the hook with {all:true} and expects callback(null, [{address,family}]). Result: every HTTPS feed fetch throws 'TypeError [ERR_INVALID_IP_ADDRESS]: Invalid IP address: undefined', which humanizeFeedError maps to the generic 'the publisher's feed is temporarily unavailable'. All sources fail.
close_reason: fixedAddressLookup now honours the {all:true} call style Node's autoSelectFamily uses; fetchValidatedHttps fixed for all outbound callers (feeds, discovery, content). Regression test added. All 434 unit tests pass.

title: Add structured server observability and health signals
description: Outside destination delivery, server failures are mostly mapped to generic client responses with no structured logs or correlation ids. Add a small redaction-safe logging and instrumentation boundary for authentication callbacks, Supabase operations, archive sync and recovery, feed fetch/parse failures, source preview, profile loads, and account deletion, plus a minimal health/readiness signal appropriate for Vercel and Supabase.
acceptance_criteria: Every critical server path emits structured success/failure signals with route, operation, duration, status class, correlation id, and safe identifiers; secrets, tokens, private notes, captured content, and raw personal data are never logged; unexpected errors remain diagnosable while client responses stay non-sensitive; health and alert thresholds are documented and smoke-tested.
close_reason: src/lib/serverLog.ts observability boundary: instrument(ctx, fn) emits one JSON line per critical op with route/operation/durationMs/statusClass/correlationId (correlationId from x-request-id / x-vercel-id when present); redact() + scrubMessage() keep secrets/tokens/JWTs/notes/content/PII out of logs; client responses unchanged. deliveryLog.ts now re-exports it. Wired into archive GET/sync, account deletion, Notion OAuth callback, feeds GET/POST, source preview. GET /api/health readiness (config + Supabase reachability) -> 200 ok / 503 degraded, body is names+booleans+durations only; HEAD = liveness. npm run smoke:health (SMOKE_BASE_URL aware) — verified live against next start: 'Health: ok in 82ms'. Alert thresholds documented in README Observability section. Tests: serverLog.test.mjs (9), healthCheck.test.mjs (3). Follow-up filed for instrumenting the remaining routes. Gates: 418 unit + 58 UI + 273 pgTAP, tsc/lint/build clean.

title: Bind and consume Notion OAuth state with the signed-in account
description: The Notion callback trusts an HMAC bearer state containing ownerId and does not verify the current Coeus session. Its random nonce is neither stored nor consumed, despite the replay-protection comment. A stolen state can authorize a connection for the embedded owner during its validity window. Bind callback completion to the initiating signed-in account and make state single-use.
acceptance_criteria: Callback requires a valid Coeus session matching the state owner; state is unguessable, expires, and is consumed once; replay and cross-account completion fail before token exchange or storage; OAuth denial remains user-friendly; tests cover missing session, mismatched account, replay, expiration, and success.
close_reason: Bound Notion OAuth callbacks to the initiating session and atomically consume persisted state.

title: Classify sync failures and protect the durable client queue
description: SyncedArchiveRepository maps every exception and non-success response to offline and retries every five seconds forever, including authorization failures, invalid contracts, and permanent server errors. Corrupt persisted queue JSON is silently replaced, losing pending operations without warning. Introduce retryable/permanent/auth states, bounded backoff, validated queue persistence, and user-visible recovery/export behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 401/403, validation 4xx, retryable 409/429/5xx/network failures, and malformed responses have distinct behavior; retries use bounded exponential backoff with jitter and honor Retry-After; permanent failures do not loop forever; corrupt queue state is preserved for recovery or explicitly surfaced before replacement; tests cover each class and reload persistence.
close_reason: SyncedArchiveRepository now classifies failures: auth (401/403), validation (permanent 4xx), retryable (408/409/429/5xx/network), malformed (bad JSON/schema/empty result). Permanent failures pause auto-sync (status error/auth_required, paused:true) and require retrySync() — no infinite loop. Retryable failures use bounded exponential backoff with half jitter honoring Retry-After (syncFailure.ts, reuses httpRetry.parseRetryAfterMs). Corrupt/malformed queue JSON is copied to coeus.archive.sync-queue.v1.corrupt and flagged (recoveredCorruptQueue) before a fresh queue replaces it; exportQueue() surfaces it. ArchiveApp shows the message, a recovery alert, and a Retry button. Tests: syncFailure.test.mjs (5) + syncedArchiveRepository.test.mjs (+9: each class, backoff, Retry-After, corrupt preserve, reload persistence). Gates: 402 unit + 58 UI + 261 pgTAP, tsc/lint/build clean.

title: Define archive quotas, sync rate limits, and revision retention
description: Each accepted sync writes another complete JSON snapshot while retaining all revisions and operation rows. The API caps one request at 2 MiB and 500 operations but has no per-user rate limit, archive entity/string quota, maximum stored snapshot size, or implemented retention policy. This enables storage amplification and unbounded GET/sync latency before the product has real users.
acceptance_criteria: Document and enforce per-account archive and request budgets at authoritative server/database boundaries; abusive sync frequency is limited across instances; snapshot size and entity/string limits are explicit; revision/operation retention preserves the promised recovery window and export semantics; monitoring can report storage growth; migration and pgTAP/unit tests cover boundary and retention behavior.
close_reason: Per-account budgets enforced at the DB boundary (archive_revisions_budget trigger: 5000 items / 2000 collections / 5000 posts / 8 MiB snapshot) and mirrored in the service-role sync store via checkArchiveBudget (adds 20k-char string-field cap) -> 413. Durable cross-instance sync rate limit: archive_sync_rate table + consume_archive_sync_budget RPC (60 req / 5 min), wired into handleArchiveSync -> 429 + Retry-After. Revision retention: prune_archive_revisions / prune_all_archive_revisions (keep last 50 AND last 30 days; current revision never pruned), run by the daily cron worker route. archive_storage_stats() function for storage-growth monitoring. Constants in src/lib/archiveBudget.ts; documented in README. Tests: archiveBudget.test.mjs (5), archiveApi.test.mjs (+2: 429/413), archive_quotas_retention.test.sql pgTAP (12). Gates: 409 unit + 58 UI + 273 pgTAP, tsc/lint/build clean.

Add robots/sitemap/canonical metadata decisions for public profiles and collections.

title: Delete profile media during cloud account deletion
description: ArchiveRecoveryStore.deleteAccount removes private archive snapshots before deleting auth.users, but it never removes files in the public profile-media bucket. Those objects have no foreign-key cascade and can remain publicly reachable after account deletion.
acceptance_criteria: Account deletion removes every owned profile-media and archive-snapshot object before or through a recoverable deletion workflow; partial storage failures are handled explicitly; no object outside the caller uid prefix can be removed; tests cover avatar, cover, replaced/orphan media, empty buckets, and failure behavior.

title: Make destination delivery concurrency-safe and observable
description: Every archive sync can start an after-hook worker while cron and manual sync can run concurrently. There is no durable per-destination lease, so two Notion runs can both observe no externalRef and create duplicate pages. The hourly budget is constructed per invocation and therefore does not rate-limit separate runs. The post-sync route discards thrown errors and the worker result failure list, and outbound adapter fetches lack explicit timeouts.
acceptance_criteria: Only one delivery run can own a destination at a time across instances; retries are durable/idempotent and do not duplicate Notion pages; rate limiting persists across invocations; adapter requests have timeouts/backoff; post-sync, manual, and cron paths expose structured outcomes without failing archive sync; operational logs contain correlation ids but no tokens or private archive content; tests cover overlap, failure, and recovery.
close_reason: Durable per-destination lease (acquire/release_destination_delivery_lease) gives cross-instance mutual exclusion + cross-invocation rate limit (min-interval); overlapping runs can no longer both create a Notion page. Adapters now use fetchWithRetry (per-request AbortSignal timeout + bounded backoff, Retry-After aware). Worker tick never throws: per-destination structured outcomes in WorkerTickResult.results; post-sync after() hook logs failures with a correlation id instead of swallowing them; manual sync route returns the summary; cron returns it. New deliveryLog.ts emits redaction-safe JSON lines (no tokens/archive content). Tests: destinationWorker.test.mjs (overlap/failure/recovery), httpRetry.test.mjs (timeout/retry/backoff), destination_delivery_lease.test.sql pgTAP. Gates: 388 unit + 58 UI + 261 pgTAP, tsc/lint/build clean.

title: canSeeIndirect() + indirect-revocation tests
description:
The correctness centre of Phase 3, and the easiest thing in the whole plan to forget.

A repost or a like references someone elses object. When that object visibility is later lowered - a public collection set to private - the repost row still exists and still points at it. If the read path checks only the repost visibility, the reposters profile leaks the existence, title and link of a collection its owner has since made private.

So visibility resolves TWICE per indirect row: once for the repost or like itself, once for the CURRENT state of its target.
design:
Add to src/lib/visibility.ts:

  export function canSeeIndirect(
    row: { visibility: Visibility },
    target: { visibility: Visibility; ownerId: string } | null,
    viewer: Viewer,
    viewerFollowsTargetOwner: boolean
  ): boolean

Rules:
- target null (deleted or orphaned) means false, always. This is what makes the orphan sweep a hygiene task rather than a correctness dependency.
- Both the row and the target must pass. The viewer relationship to the TARGET owner is what matters for the target check, not their relationship to the reposter - these are different people and conflating them is the specific bug this function exists to prevent.
- A repost of a followers-only collection is visible only to someone who follows the COLLECTION owner, even if they follow the reposter.

The read path must therefore join the target row and its owner, not just the target id. Note that in the query design for task 3.3 and 3.4 - a lazy implementation that reads only the denormalised title and url from the repost row would silently bypass this entire function, which is why reposts store NO denormalised copy of their target.

Tests in visibility.test.mjs: the full matrix of row visibility times target visibility times viewer relationship to each of the two owners, plus the null-target case. Include an explicit named test for the revocation scenario end to end.
acceptance_criteria:
- canSeeIndirect returns false whenever the target is null.
- A repost of a collection later set to private is invisible to everyone but the reposter.
- Following the reposter does NOT grant visibility of a followers-only target owned by someone else.
- reposts and likes store no denormalised copy of their target title or url.
- The revocation scenario has its own named test.
notes: Risk R6 in docs/profile-page-plan.md. Depends on canSee from 2.2 and the tables from 3.1.
close_reason: canSeeIndirect(row, target, viewer, viewerFollowsTargetOwner) in src/lib/visibility.ts: null target => false unconditionally; step 1 row check vs viewer↔actor; actor (owner) always sees own rows; step 2 target check vs viewer↔target-owner via viewerToward(). 12 new visibility.test.mjs cases incl. named revocation scenario + full public-row×target×target-owner-relationship matrix. 21 visibility tests green.

title: API: /api/posts publish + unpublish, and PATCH profile sections
description:
Two endpoints.

/api/posts - publish and unpublish a post, calling the publish_post / unpublish_post RPCs from task 2.4 through derivePostSnapshot from task 2.5. The server derives the public-safe payload from its own archive data; the client sends only the item id, the chosen visibility and the commentary. This mirrors exactly how /api/collections/publish works today - the client never sends the snapshot.

PATCH /api/account/profile/sections - the five show_* booleans and likes_visibility. A partial update, separate from the main profile PUT, because toggling a switch should not require sending the whole profile.
acceptance_criteria:
- Publishing a post the caller does not own returns 404, not 500.
- The client cannot influence any field of the stored post beyond itemLocalId, visibility and commentary.
- PATCH sections rejects unknown keys and likesVisibility of unlisted.
- An empty PATCH body returns 400.
- visibleSections hides the count as well as the list for non-owners, and marks rather than hides for the owner.
- Handlers unit-tested with a fake store.
close_reason: Two endpoints. /api/posts/publish + /unpublish: thin routes -> handlePublishPost/handleUnpublishPost -> SupabasePostPublicationStore, which reads the owner's own archive snapshot, finds the item by local id (PostItemNotFoundError -> 404, never 500), derives via derivePostSnapshot, validates via parsePostSnapshot, then calls the publish_post/unpublish_post RPCs. Client sends only {itemLocalId, visibility, commentary}; any extra field is a 400. PATCH /api/account/profile/sections: profileSections.ts pure module (parseProfileSectionsPatch rejects unknown keys + likesVisibility unlisted + empty body; visibleSections(switches, viewer) marks-for-owner / hides-entirely-for-others incl. count), ProfileStore.updateSections partial update, 404 pre-onboarding. 40 new unit tests (fake stores), 308 suite green, tsc + eslint clean.

title: API: /api/profiles/follow, /unfollow, /followed
description:
The person-follow endpoints. Mirror the three existing collection endpoints - /api/collections/follow, /unfollow and /followed - in structure, error shape and cache headers, so the client-side follow button can be a near-copy of the existing one.

Critically, keep the 401 response shape identical: FollowButton.tsx already special-cases status 401 to render a sign-in prompt rather than a generic failure, and ProfileFollowButton (task 2.9) should inherit that behaviour for free.
design:
Follow the existing split: a pure handler module (src/lib/profileFollowApi.ts) taking a dependencies object, and thin route files that construct the dependencies. That is the pattern every API route in this project uses (see collectionPublicationApi.ts + the routes under src/app/api/collections/), and it is what makes the handlers testable without Next.

POST /api/profiles/follow   body { profileId } - a uuid, validated with the same isUuid helper shape parseFollowRequest uses.
POST /api/profiles/unfollow body { profileId }
GET  /api/profiles/followed - returns { profiles: [...] } for the caller.

Reject a self-follow with 422 rather than relying on the database check to surface as a 500.

Store methods go on a new SupabaseProfileFollowStore, or extend SupabaseProfileStore - prefer a separate store, since ProfileStore has a clean two-method interface worth keeping small.

Tests in src/lib/profileFollowApi.test.mjs with a fake store, matching collectionPublicationApi.test.mjs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unauthenticated requests get 401 with the same body shape the collection endpoints return.
- Following the same profile twice is idempotent, not an error.
- Self-follow returns 422.
- A malformed or non-uuid profileId returns 400.
- /followed returns only the caller own follows and sets private, no-store cache headers.
- Handlers are unit-tested with a fake store, no database.
close_reason: Person-follow endpoints: pure parser (profileFollow.ts), SupabaseProfileFollowStore (upsert ignoreDuplicates / delete / embedded listFollowed), handlers (profileFollowApi.ts) mirroring collection follow endpoints — identical 401 {error} shape, private/no-store headers, 400 on bad uuid/JSON, 422 self-follow guard before the store, 204 idempotent follow/unfollow. Three thin routes under src/app/api/profiles/. 16 unit tests (fake store), tsc + eslint clean, 270 unit suite green.

title: archiveTypes + archiveValidation: add followers, retire the friends audience
description:
Widen the client-side content types for the new visibility model, and retire SocialPost.audience "friends".

CollectionVisibility in src/lib/archiveTypes.ts gains "followers". SocialAudience is replaced by the shared Visibility type - "friends" has no meaning under a model where followers means your followers rather than mutuals.

This changes the SYNCED ARCHIVE SNAPSHOT SCHEMA, which is data clients own and write. Existing snapshots in archive_revisions carry audience: "friends" today. A validator that hard-rejects it would brick an existing archive on load, so the reader must be tolerant.
design:
src/lib/archiveTypes.ts:
- CollectionVisibility becomes "private" | "followers" | "unlisted" | "public" (or simply reuse Visibility from visibility.ts).
- SocialAudience is removed; SocialPost.audience becomes Visibility.

src/lib/archiveValidation.ts, the two lines that matter:
- line 52, the collection visibility allowlist, gains "followers".
- line 66, which currently rejects anything that is not "public" or "friends", becomes: accept the four Visibility values, AND accept the legacy "friends", mapping it to "followers" on read.

TOLERANT READ, MIGRATE ON WRITE. Never reject. The mapping happens in the validator so every caller gets the normalised value and no downstream code needs to know the legacy value existed. The next save writes the normalised value, so the legacy value drains out of the corpus naturally without a backfill.

Also check src/lib/archiveSync.ts line 93, which lists the socialPost field names for the sync protocol - the field name audience does not change, only its value domain, so that list should need no edit. Confirm rather than assume.

Add a test asserting that a snapshot containing audience: "friends" parses successfully and yields "followers".
acceptance_criteria:
- A snapshot containing audience "friends" parses and normalises to "followers".
- A snapshot containing an unknown audience value is still rejected.
- Collection visibility "followers" is accepted.
- No existing archiveValidation or archiveSync test regresses.
- The legacy mapping is covered by an explicit test with a comment explaining why it cannot be removed until the corpus has drained.
notes: Risk R4 in docs/profile-page-plan.md.
close_reason: archiveTypes: CollectionVisibility = Visibility (gains followers), SocialPost.audience = Visibility, SocialAudience removed. archiveValidation: isVisibility guard for collection visibility; LEGACY_AUDIENCE map normalises friends->followers on read, flags result migrated (no backfill, drains on next save). archiveSync line 93 confirmed unchanged (field name only). 5 new tests; 258 unit + 23 ui pass; eslint + tsc clean.

title: lib/post.ts: derivePostSnapshot() boundary + absence tests
description:
The publish boundary for posts - the same contract derivePublicationSnapshot() provides for collection items, and the reason a post can safely leave the private archive.

Takes an ArchiveItem plus the owner explicit choices and returns only the fields that may be published. The private fields on ArchiveItem - note, tags, state, starred, topic, savedAt, articleId - must never cross, exactly as they never cross derivePublicationSnapshot().
design:
export interface PostSnapshot {
    itemLocalId, title, url, sourceName, author, excerpt, commentary, visibility
  }
  export function derivePostSnapshot(item: ArchiveItem, options: { visibility, commentary }): PostSnapshot
  export function parsePostSnapshot(raw: unknown): PostParseResult

Mirror collectionPublication.ts closely, including the length caps (title 500, excerpt 2000, commentary 4000) and the isHttpUrl / isBoundedString helpers - either import them or duplicate the pattern, but do not invent a third validation style.

Critically: commentary comes from options, NOT from item.note. item.note is the private annotation and must never be published. derivePublicationSnapshot already makes this distinction explicit in its doc comment for curatorComments; carry the same comment across so the reason survives.

Tests in src/lib/post.test.mjs, modelled on collectionPublication.test.mjs. The load-bearing test constructs an ArchiveItem with every private field populated with a recognisable sentinel and asserts NONE of those sentinels appear anywhere in JSON.stringify of the snapshot.
acceptance_criteria:
- derivePostSnapshot is pure and imports nothing server-only.
- commentary is sourced from options and never from item.note.
- A test asserts that note, tags, state, starred, topic, savedAt and articleId sentinels are absent from the serialized snapshot.
- parsePostSnapshot rejects unknown fields, a non-http url, and over-length text, matching parsePublicationSnapshot behaviour.
close_reason: src/lib/post.ts: derivePostSnapshot() publish boundary + parsePostSnapshot() validation, mirroring collectionPublication.ts (same isHttpUrl/isBoundedString/isRecord pattern, caps title 500 / excerpt 2000 / commentary 4000, reuses PublicationVisibility). commentary comes from options, never item.note. 10 tests incl. the load-bearing sentinel test: note/tags/state/starred/topic/savedAt/articleId absent from JSON.stringify. tsc + eslint clean.

title: Migration C: posts table + publish_post / unpublish_post RPCs
description:
Give posts a server-readable home. Today SocialPost exists only inside ArchiveData, serialized whole into archive_revisions.snapshot under owner-only RLS and authored client-side. There is no posts table and no publish boundary for one, which is exactly why the Posts tab could not ship in Phase 1.

A post is one sourced clip: a URL with optional commentary, the link always attached. So the table mirrors collection_publication_items field for field, plus an author, a visibility and timestamps.
design:
create table public.posts (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  author_id uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  item_local_id text not null check (char_length(item_local_id) between 1 and 160),
  title text not null check (char_length(title) between 1 and 500),
  url text not null check (url ~ "^https?://"),
  source_name text not null default "" check (char_length(source_name) <= 200),
  author text not null default "" check (char_length(author) <= 200),
  excerpt text not null default "" check (char_length(excerpt) <= 2000),
  commentary text not null default "" check (char_length(commentary) <= 4000),
  visibility public.visibility not null default "private",
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (author_id, item_local_id)
);
create index posts_author_live_idx on public.posts (author_id, created_at desc);

Note the default: private. Coeus is private by default, and a post row that appears before its author has chosen a visibility must not be public.

RLS follows collection_publications: a permissive select for rows whose visibility is unlisted or public, a select for the owner over all their own rows, and NO direct insert/update/delete - writes go through security-definer RPCs, revoked from public/anon/authenticated and granted to service_role, exactly as publish_collection is.

publish_post(p_owner_id, p_item_local_id, p_visibility, p_title, p_url, p_source_name, p_author, p_excerpt, p_commentary) and unpublish_post(p_owner_id, p_item_local_id). Model them on publish_collection / unpublish_collection including the owner guard that raises when the caller does not own the target.

The followers tier cannot be expressed in a simple RLS select policy without a subquery against profile_follows. Since every read goes through the admin client and canSee(), keep the RLS policy at the unlisted/public level as defense-in-depth and let canSee do the real work - the same division of labour getBySlug() already documents.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table, indexes and RPCs exist; direct writes from anon and authenticated are rejected.
- publish_post refuses to write a post for an author_id the caller does not own.
- Default visibility is private.
- A republish of the same (author_id, item_local_id) updates rather than duplicating.
- pgTAP covers the owner guard, the grant set, and the select policy.
notes: Finding 01 in docs/profile-page-plan.md. Depends on the visibility type from 2.1.
close_reason: 20260906150000_posts.sql: posts table (private default, unique(author_id,item_local_id), posts_author_live_idx), RLS select-only at unlisted/public + author-own, no write policies. publish_post/unpublish_post security-definer, owner guard raises 'Profile not found for owner', revoked from public/anon/authenticated, granted service_role. supabase/tests/posts.test.sql: 24 pgTAP assertions, all 150 db tests pass after db reset.

title: Migration B: profile_follows + show_* switches + likes_visibility
description:
The person-level follow graph, plus the profile-level display settings that govern which sections appear.

profile_follows is the new primary social edge. It is what makes the followers visibility tier meaningful - until now the only follow in the system was collection_follows, a subscription to a published collection, which is a different relationship.

followers means YOUR followers, not mutuals. A follow is one-directional and needs no acceptance.
design:
create table public.profile_follows (
  follower_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  followee_id uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (follower_id, followee_id),
  check (follower_id <> followee_id)
);
create index profile_follows_followee_idx on public.profile_follows (followee_id, created_at desc);
create index profile_follows_follower_idx on public.profile_follows (follower_id, created_at desc);

RLS mirrors collection_follows exactly (20260904150000_collection_follows.sql): followers manage their own rows under a for-all policy keyed on follower_id = auth.uid(). Add a separate permissive select policy so follower counts are readable - and note in the migration comment that the show_* switches do NOT gate this at the database level, because reads go through the admin client and the gate is applied in the view layer.

alter table public.profiles add:
  likes_visibility public.visibility not null default "public"
    check (likes_visibility <> "unlisted"),   -- unlisted is meaningless for a list
  show_followers boolean not null default true,
  show_following boolean not null default true,
  show_reposts   boolean not null default true,
  show_replies   boolean not null default true,
  show_likes     boolean not null default true;

Defaults are true because these sections only ever contain content the object-level visibility already permits.

Note: follower_id references auth.users, not profiles, matching collection_follows - an account can follow before completing onboarding. Any UI listing followers must therefore tolerate a follower with no profile row and omit it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A user can follow and unfollow another profile; a duplicate follow is idempotent.
- Self-follow is rejected by the check constraint.
- Deleting an account removes both its outgoing and incoming follows.
- likes_visibility rejects unlisted.
- Follower and following counts are queryable with an index-only scan on the new indexes.
- pgTAP covers self-follow rejection, cross-account write rejection, and cascade on delete.
close_reason: Migration 20260906160000_profile_follows.sql + pgTAP (18 tests, suite 168 green after db reset): profile_follows edge with mirrored collection_follows RLS (FOR ALL own-rows + permissive SELECT for counts), self-follow check, both listing indexes, cascade on account and profile delete; profiles gains likes_visibility (rejects unlisted) + five show_* switches defaulting true.

title: lib/visibility.ts: canSee() + the sixteen-cell truth table
description:
The second security-critical pure module. Every read path in Phase 2 and Phase 3 funnels through it, so it exists once, in one file, with total test coverage.

Export the Visibility type, a Viewer union, and canSee(objectVisibility, viewer). Four visibilities times four viewer kinds is sixteen cells - a single exhaustive test, no database, no ambiguity about any case.

Also export the distinction this codebase must not lose: canSee is a SECURITY decision. The profiles.show_* switches are a DISPLAY preference. They live in a different module (profileSections.ts) precisely so nobody mistakes a boolean column for a permission.
acceptance_criteria:
- canSee is pure, imports nothing, and covers all sixteen cells.
- The test states the full table literally, not by generation.
- isListable excludes unlisted from listings for every non-owner viewer.
- The module comment states plainly that show_* switches are display-only and live elsewhere.
- Every Phase 2 read path calls canSee or isListable rather than comparing visibility strings inline.
notes: Risk R7 in docs/profile-page-plan.md.
close_reason: lib/visibility.ts: canSee + isListable + isVisibility, pure (imports nothing). src/lib/visibility.test.mjs asserts the full 16-cell truth table literally. Module comment states show_* switches are display-only and live in profileSections.ts. All 254 unit tests pass, tsc clean.

title: [Phase 2] Visibility model, person graph, posts
description:
The largest phase and the one everything downstream waits on. Three things land together because they are mutually dependent: the four-value visibility enum, the person-level follow graph, and the first content type Coeus publishes outside a collection.

The four-value enum is private, followers, unlisted, public. private means only you. followers means you and your followers - YOUR followers, not mutuals. unlisted means anyone with the link, but off-profile and off-Discover. public means everyone and Discover-eligible.

Likes are NOT tagged per row: one profiles.likes_visibility setting governs the whole Likes list. Profile-level section switches (show_followers, show_following, show_reposts, show_replies, show_likes) govern both the count and the list, stacked on top of per-object visibility - they are DISPLAY controls, not security boundaries.

Posts land here rather than Phase 1 because they have no server-readable home today: SocialPost lives only inside the private archive_revisions.snapshot blob and has never crossed a publish boundary.
design:
Three migrations that must land in order: A (enum), B (graph + switches), C (posts). A is the highest-blast-radius migration in the whole plan.

Two pure modules carry the correctness: src/lib/visibility.ts (canSee) and src/lib/post.ts (derivePostSnapshot). Both are unit-tested with no database.

Retire SocialPost.audience "friends": followers means your followers, not mutuals, so the value has no meaning under the new model. Existing archive snapshots carrying it must be tolerated on read.
acceptance_criteria:
- A person can be followed, and following feeds a Following view on /discover.
- A collection or post set to followers is visible to a follower and invisible to a stranger, proven by pgTAP AND by the canSee truth table.
- Switching off a section removes both its tab and its count for visitors, and greys the tab for the owner.
- Posts render on the profile behind the same kind of derive boundary collections use.
- No existing published collection changes visibility as a result of the migration.
close_reason: Phase 2 complete: visibility model wired end to end, person-follow graph + Following view, posts (tab + composer). 14/14 children closed. Exit criteria met.

title: UI: ProfileBanner, ProfileSidebar, ProfileTabs + src/styles/profile.css
description:
The read-only surface, as server components. No client JavaScript in this task.

ProfileBanner: full-bleed cover (generative field or uploaded photo), the scrim, the square avatar overlapping the lower-left, and the identity block (display name, @handle, location) set over it.

ProfileTabs: the tab + actions row under the banner. Tabs are links carrying ?tab=. Phase 1 renders Overview and Collections live; Posts, Reposts, Replies and Likes are omitted entirely this phase rather than rendered dead.

ProfileSidebar: the persistent right column - the figures row, bio, external links. The Likes strip is Phase 3 and is omitted, not stubbed.

Styling is a new hand-rolled stylesheet, matching the project convention (no CSS framework).
design:
src/styles/profile.css, imported from src/app/globals.css alongside the existing eight sheets. Use ONLY the tokens already defined in src/styles/base.css - --bg, --fg, --muted, --border, --line, --handle, --accent, --radius (which is 0), the spacing scale and the type scale. Do not introduce new colour literals; a profile page that does not respond to the existing theme and palette switches (data-theme, data-palette) is a bug.

Layout from the mockup: a two-column body, grid-template-columns minmax(0, 1fr) 19rem, collapsing to a single column under 780px with the sidebar ordered first. The banner is 232px desktop, 200px mobile, avatar 104px desktop and 78px mobile.

The generative cover renders as a pre element with aria-hidden, fed by generativeCover() from task 1.6.

Accessibility: the tab row is a real list of links (not role=tablist, since these are navigations, not in-page panels); the avatar is decorative and aria-hidden because the display name is already adjacent text; the banner identity block must keep contrast against both cover modes, which is what the scrim is for.
acceptance_criteria:
- The page renders correctly in light and dark themes and under each palette in base.css.
- No horizontal scroll at 320px width.
- Cover, avatar, identity, tabs, figures, bio and links all render from real data.
- Zero client JavaScript from these three components.
- Tab links change the rendered panel via ?tab= with no client navigation required.
notes: Depends on 1.8 for the view data and 1.6 for the generative cover.
close_reason:
ProfileBanner (cover: uploaded or aria-hidden generative 
; overlapping avatar or initials; name/@handle/location), ProfileTabs (Overview+Collections only this phase, ?tab= links, owner Edit-profile action), ProfileSidebar (figures + bio + links; Followers labelled 'Coll. followers'), ProfileCollections (cards, unlisted/unpublished flags), ProfileView. src/styles/profile.css imported from globals.css — base.css tokens only, no colour literals; two-col body collapsing at 780px with sidebar first; banner 232/200, avatar 104/78. Zero client JS in these. Verified rendering live via /@theman HTML. NOTE: light/dark + per-palette visual pass not run (no browser in this session) — structural guarantee is tokens-only.

title: API: extend PUT /api/account/profile + new POST /api/account/profile/media
description:
Two API changes.

1. PUT /api/account/profile carries the new fields. Same route, same handler, same validator - handleSaveProfile already funnels through validateProfileInput and already maps HandleTakenError to a 409 with field: "handle". Nothing about that structure changes; it just validates more fields.

2. POST /api/account/profile/media is new: it accepts one image, writes it to the profile-media bucket under the caller uid prefix, and returns the public URL for the client to save into avatar_url or cover_url.

The upload route is the second half of the defense described in task 1.4. The storage policy stops one account writing under another prefix; this route stops the bucket becoming a general-purpose file host.
design:
POST /api/account/profile/media
- Authenticate with authenticateArchiveRequest() - 401 otherwise, matching every other authenticated route.
- Accept multipart/form-data with a single file field and a kind field of "avatar" or "cover".
- Reject anything whose MIME type is not in an explicit allowlist (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp). Do not trust the client Content-Type alone - check the leading magic bytes as well.
- Cap size: 2 MB for an avatar, 5 MB for a cover. Reject over-size before reading the whole body where possible.
- Write via createRequestSupabaseClient() (the users own session, so the storage policy applies) to <uid>/<kind>-<random>.<ext>.
- Return { url } with the same private, no-store cache headers profileApi.ts already sets.
- Delete the previous file for that kind on success, so the bucket does not accumulate orphans.

Tests extend src/lib/profileApi.test.mjs for the PUT changes. The media route is thin enough that its logic (the allowlist, the size cap, the path construction) should be extracted into a small pure helper in profileMedia.ts or a sibling, so it can be tested without a Supabase client.
acceptance_criteria:
- PUT accepts and persists the new fields, and returns 422 with per-field errors for malformed links or an over-length location.
- POST media rejects an unauthenticated caller with 401.
- POST media rejects a non-image MIME type and a file whose magic bytes disagree with its declared type.
- POST media rejects an over-size file.
- POST media writes only under the caller uid prefix, and replacing an image removes the previous one.
- The allowlist and size-cap logic is unit-tested as a pure function.
close_reason: PUT /api/account/profile now passes location/links/avatarUrl/coverUrl/pinnedCollectionSlugs through validateProfileInput (422 with per-field errors for bad links / long location). New POST /api/account/profile/media: src/lib/profileUpload.ts (pure: MIME allowlist png/jpeg/webp, magic-byte sniff, 2MB avatar / 5MB cover caps, <uid>/<kind>-<token>.<ext> path, objectPathFromPublicUrl guards cross-account delete) + src/lib/profileMediaApi.ts (DI handler: 401, writes via caller session, best-effort orphan cleanup) + route. 34 new unit assertions across profileUpload/profileMediaApi/profileApi tests, all pass.

title: Route: src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx + /@handle rewrite + generateMetadata
description:
The page itself. A server component at src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx, reached canonically at /u/<handle> and publicly at /@<handle> via the rewrite confirmed in task 1.1.

Copy the shape of src/app/c/[slug]/page.tsx exactly - it is the established template for a public, server-rendered, admin-client-read page in this codebase: force-dynamic, a cache() wrapped loader so generateMetadata and the page body share one fetch, notFound() on a missing handle, and AppShell for chrome.

Determine isOwner by comparing authenticateArchiveRequest() against the resolved profile id, then hand both the data and the viewer to deriveProfileView() from task 1.5. The page itself does no filtering - all of it happens inside the boundary function.
acceptance_criteria:
- /@handle and /u/handle both render the same page; the browser URL is preserved on the rewrite.
- An unknown handle renders 404; a Supabase outage renders the error boundary, not 404.
- isOwner is true only when the session subject equals the profile id.
- generateMetadata returns a per-profile title and description and shares the cache() fetch with the body.
- ?tab=collections selects the Collections panel server-side; an unknown tab falls back to overview.
- The page issues no more than two database round-trips per render.
notes: Depends on 1.1 (which mechanism), 1.5 (the view type) and 1.7 (resolveHandle).
close_reason: src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx: force-dynamic, cache()'d loadProfile shared with generateMetadata, notFound() only on null (missing handle), thrown errors reach the error boundary. /@:handle rewrite in next.config.ts (task 1.1 mechanism). isOwner = session sub === profile.id. Verified against local Supabase: /@theman -> 200 with title 'bareaga (@theman) — Coeus'; /@nobody -> 404; missing-column DB error -> 500 (error boundary, not 404); ?tab=collections vs unknown->overview via resolveProfileTab. Two round-trips per render.

title: profile.ts validators + profileStore.resolveHandle / listOwnedPublications
description:
Extend the profile domain for the new fields, and add the two server reads the page needs.

In src/lib/profile.ts: add a ProfileLink type, LOCATION_MAX, validateProfileLinks(), and extend Profile, ProfileInput and validateProfileInput to carry location, links, avatarUrl, coverUrl and pinnedCollectionSlugs. HANDLE_PATTERN and BIO_MAX are untouched - the handle shape rule never varies.

In src/lib/profileStore.server.ts: add resolveHandle(handle) and listOwnedPublications(profileId).

IMPORTANT: every handle lookup in the codebase goes through resolveHandle(), starting now, even though in Phase 1 it does nothing more than a select on profiles.handle. That single indirection is the ONLY reason sub-epic 4 (handle changes with redirects) can land later without touching the page.
design:
resolveHandle returns a small envelope rather than a bare profile, so the redirect case can be added later without changing its callers:

  interface HandleResolution { profile: Profile; redirectFrom: string | null }
  resolveHandle(handle: string): Promise<HandleResolution | null>

In Phase 1 redirectFrom is always null. Sub-epic 4 fills it from handle_history.

listOwnedPublications(profileId) uses the new collection_publications.owner_id column and the collection_publications_owner_live_idx index from task 1.3 - one query, no join through archives.

Extend the COLUMNS constant and the profileRow() mapper in profileStore.server.ts for the new columns. Note the existing comment in collectionPublicationStore.server.ts about avoiding TypeScript parameter-property constructors under node --experimental-strip-types - SupabaseProfileStore already uses one, so if a test ever needs to import this module, that constructor has to be expanded first.

Tests extend src/lib/profile.test.mjs: link validation (count cap, shape, scheme), location length, and that an empty links array normalises the same way an empty bio normalises to null today.
acceptance_criteria:
- validateProfileInput accepts and normalises the new fields and rejects malformed links with a per-field error.
- More than five links, a non-https url, or an entry missing a label is rejected with errors.links set.
- resolveHandle returns { profile, redirectFrom: null } or null, and is the only handle lookup in the codebase.
- listOwnedPublications issues one query against collection_publications and does not read archives.
- profile.test.mjs extended and passing.
notes: resolveHandle is the seam for sub-epic 4. Do not let a second handle lookup appear anywhere else.
close_reason: src/lib/profile.ts: ProfileLink, LOCATION_MAX/LINKS_MAX/etc, validateProfileLinks() (mirrors the DB check), normalizePinnedSlugs(); Profile/ProfileInput/validateProfileInput extended with location/links/avatarUrl/coverUrl/pinnedCollectionSlugs. src/lib/profileStore.server.ts: resolveHandle(handle) -> {profile, redirectFrom:null} (THE only handle lookup in the codebase — the sub-epic 4 seam) and listOwnedPublications(profileId) — one PostgREST query on owner_id with item+follower counts embedded, no archives join. profile.test.mjs extended (link cap/shape/scheme, location, pinned normalisation). Verified live.

title: lib/publicProfile.ts: deriveProfileView() public-safe boundary + tests
description:
The single most important file in Phase 1. This is the profile analogue of derivePublicationSnapshot() in src/lib/collectionPublication.ts: the one place where profile data crosses from "everything the server knows" to "what may be rendered for this viewer".

Export a PublicProfileView type and deriveProfileView(profile, publications, viewer). The viewer is an EXPLICIT argument, not an ambient lookup, so owner-only rows are a deliberate input rather than the accident of a filter someone forgot to write.

Pure module: no server-only import, no Supabase import, no next import. That is what lets it be exhaustively tested under node --test with no database, the same way collectionPublication.test.mjs is.
design:
Shape:

  export interface ProfileViewer { isOwner: boolean }
  export interface PublicProfileView {
    handle, displayName, bio, location, links, avatarUrl, coverUrl,
    collections: ProfileCollectionCard[],
    figures: { collections, posts, followers, following },
    isOwner: boolean
  }
  export function deriveProfileView(profile, publications, viewer): PublicProfileView

Rules the function enforces:
- profile.id (the auth user uuid) NEVER crosses. The page has no need for it and it is an account identifier.
- created_at / updated_at do not cross.
- Unpublished publications (unpublished_at not null) are included only when viewer.isOwner, and are flagged so the UI can grey them.
- In Phase 1 the collections list filters on visibility in (public, unlisted) for visitors; unlisted publications appear on the owner view only. Phase 2 replaces this line with a canSee() call - leave a comment saying so.
- Figures are computed from what actually crossed, never from a raw count, so the number can never imply a row the viewer cannot reach.

Tests go in src/lib/publicProfile.test.mjs. The load-bearing test asserts ABSENCE: given a profile carrying id and timestamps, assert those keys are not present on the returned view. Testing that the public fields are present catches nothing.
acceptance_criteria:
- deriveProfileView is pure and imports nothing server-only.
- A visitor view omits profile.id, timestamps and every unpublished collection.
- An owner view includes unpublished collections, flagged.
- Figures always equal the length of what actually crossed the boundary.
- A test asserts specific private keys are ABSENT from the visitor view.
- Runs under npm run test:unit with no database.
notes: Mirrors the boundary and the test style of src/lib/collectionPublication.ts and collectionPublication.test.mjs. Depends on 1.2 and 1.3 for the field and column shapes.
close_reason: src/lib/publicProfile.ts: deriveProfileView(profile, publications, viewer, options). Pure (no server-only/supabase/next). profile.id + timestamps never cross (load-bearing absence test asserts the uuid is not in JSON.stringify(view)). Visitor sees live public collections only; owner sees unlisted + unpublished (flagged). figures.collections === collections.length; followers sums live collections' follower counts unless overridden; posts=0. 11 tests in publicProfile.test.mjs pass. Verified live: /@theman renders figures from real DB.

title: Migration: denormalize owner_id onto collection_publications + backfill + index
description:
collection_publications keys on archive_id only. Listing "the collections published by @handle" therefore requires walking profiles.id to archives.owner_id to archives.id to collection_publications.archive_id - three hops ending in a table whose RLS is owner-only, on the hot path of a public page, with no supporting index.

Add owner_id to collection_publications, backfill it from archives, mark it not null, and index it for the profile query. This is a prerequisite for task 1.5 and it is the reason the profile page can render collections with one indexed query instead of a join through private data.

title: Migration: profiles surface columns (avatar, cover, location, links, pinned order)
description:
Extend public.profiles with the fields the profile page renders. The table today (supabase/migrations/20260905132000_profiles.sql) carries only id, handle, display_name, bio and timestamps.

Add: avatar_url text, cover_url text (null means render the generative cover), location text, links jsonb not null default the empty array, pinned_collection_slugs text[] not null default the empty array.

design:
Constraints to add:
- location: char_length <= 80
- links: a jsonb array, at most 5 entries, each entry an object carrying label and url keys, with url matching ^https?://. Express this with jsonb_array_length plus a check over jsonb_array_elements, or a small immutable helper function if the inline check gets unreadable.
- avatar_url / cover_url: must be null or start with the public URL prefix of the profile-media bucket, so a profile row can never point the page at an arbitrary third-party host.

No new index is needed for handle lookups: profiles.handle is already unique, which gives a usable index for free.

The profiles_touch_updated_at trigger already exists and covers the new columns automatically.

pgTAP goes in supabase/tests/profile_surface.test.sql and follows the structure of the existing supabase/tests/profiles.test.sql.

- Migration applies cleanly against a fresh supabase db reset.
- A links value with 6 entries, a non-array links value, and an entry missing url are each rejected.
- A location longer than 80 characters is rejected.
- An avatar_url pointing outside the profile-media bucket is rejected.
- Existing profile rows survive the migration with the new columns at their defaults.

title: Spike: verify the /@:handle rewrite parses in Next 16
description:
Confirm that Next 16.3.4 accepts a rewrite whose source is /@:handle - a bare @ literal immediately preceding a path parameter. This is an unusual pattern for path-to-regexp and it gates the entire route design, so it is resolved FIRST and cheaply rather than discovered during implementation.

Add the rewrite to next.config.ts, add a throwaway src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx that renders the handle, run next dev, and request /@testhandle. Confirm the handle param arrives intact and without the @.

Also confirm the interaction with src/proxy.ts: its matcher currently excludes only api, _next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico and image extensions, so /@handle DOES pass through the proxy. Confirm no redirect fires and the Supabase getClaims() refresh still works on this path.
design:
next.config.ts already exports a NextConfig with a turbopack.root entry; add rewrites alongside it:

  async rewrites() { return [{ source: "/@:handle", destination: "/u/:handle" }]; }

Per node_modules/next/dist/docs/.../rewrites.md the route order is headers, redirects, proxy, beforeFiles rewrites, static files, afterFiles rewrites, dynamic routes, fallback. A plain array is applied at the afterFiles position, which is correct here: nothing in public/ or the static routes can shadow /@something.

FALLBACK if the source does not parse: do the rewrite in src/proxy.ts with NextResponse.rewrite(). The proxy already runs on this path and already clones the URL for its redirects, so the change is about six lines. Record which path was taken in the issue notes - Phase 1 task 1.8 depends on knowing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Requesting /@testhandle renders the placeholder page with handle === "testhandle".
- The browser URL stays /@testhandle (a rewrite, not a redirect).
- Requesting /u/testhandle directly also renders (the canonical path stays reachable).
- src/proxy.ts still refreshes the auth cookie on this path and does not redirect.
- The chosen mechanism (next.config rewrite vs proxy rewrite) is recorded in this issue notes before closing.
notes:
RESOLVED via next.config.ts rewrite (not the proxy fallback). Added `async rewrites() { return [{ source: '/@:handle', destination: '/u/:handle' }]; }`. Verified against the running dev server (Next 16.3.4, Turbopack, which hot-reloaded the config):
- GET /@testhandle -> 200, no redirect, renders handle === 'testhandle' (the @ is stripped, param intact)
- Browser URL stays /@testhandle (rewrite, not redirect: redirect_url empty)
- GET /u/testhandle -> 200, canonical path still reachable
- proxy.ts still runs on this path (matcher excludes only api/_next/static/_next/image/favicon.ico/image-ext; /@handle matches) and issues no redirect
- Static routes unaffected: /about /discover / /signin all still 200 (plain-array rewrites apply at afterFiles, after the filesystem)
'@' is not in path-to-regexp's special-char set (rewrites.md:223), so /@:handle parses as literal-@ + :handle param with no escaping. Task 1.8 keeps this rewrite; placeholder page at src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx is marked SPIKE PLACEHOLDER for 1.8 to replace.
close_reason: Spike passed: /@:handle rewrite works via next.config.ts; no proxy fallback needed. Mechanism recorded in notes.

title: [Phase 1] Profile page: identity, route, published collections

Deliberately scoped to data the app can ALREADY publish. No person-follow graph, no new visibility model, no posts, likes, reposts or replies, no show_* switches. That restraint is what makes this phase shippable in one pass.

The Followers figure in this phase counts COLLECTION followers - an aggregate over this owner collection_follows rows - and is labelled as such in the UI, because that is genuinely what it counts until Phase 2 replaces it with the person graph.

title: Surface local persistence and action failures
description:
## Problem
Preference and archive autosaves are fire-and-forget, so localStorage or validation rejection leaves optimistic UI and success feedback without durable state. Native share or clipboard errors and slash command exceptions are also silent. Add explicit persistence and action status with retry where meaningful, while keeping expected AbortError cancellation quiet.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Make localStorage writes reject, for example through a quota or security failure.
2. Change a preference or archive item and observe optimistic UI without an error; reload restores older durable state.
3. Make clipboard sharing reject or a slash command throw and observe no user-facing failure message.
acceptance_criteria: Local preference/archive write failures are visible and recoverable; action success is not emitted before durable acceptance; share cancellation is distinguished from failure; slash command failure is announced; rejection paths have tests.
notes: Added queued preference/archive persistence status, visible failure feedback, and retry controls. Slash and share errors are surfaced rather than silently swallowed. Added queue and interaction tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Build accessible overlay and mobile sheet foundation
description: ShareSheet and SlashMenu claim modal semantics without complete focus containment/restoration or background inertness; ShareSheet lacks Escape and scroll lock; mobile Settings visually becomes a sheet without adaptive dialog behavior or safe-area padding. Implement a shared, tested overlay foundation while preserving desktop Settings as a deliberate nonmodal popover if desired.
acceptance_criteria: Modal overlays set initial focus, contain Tab/Shift+Tab, handle Escape, restore opener focus, prevent background activation/scroll, and support safe-area insets; Slash Enter handling is scoped; mobile Settings semantics match its modality; automated interaction tests cover these behaviors.
notes: Added shared modal behavior for focus trapping/restoration, Escape, inert background, scroll lock, initial focus, and mobile safe areas; applied to Settings, ShareSheet, and SlashMenu. Added interaction tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Make Discover save and follow states truthful
description:
## Problem
The Discover Save control is a no-op for items already structurally present in the archive, while collection follows are hard-coded component state, reset on reload, and do not affect the feed despite preview copy saying they live on the device. Define preview versus production semantics and make all labels and state behavior accurate.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Discover and toggle a collection Follow state.
2. Reload and observe that the hard-coded default state returns; also observe that the feed never changes with the toggle.
3. Activate Save on any Discover post and observe that only a notice changes and no archive mutation occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Save is an accurate disabled/already-saved state or performs a real durable save; Follow either persists and filters the feed or is explicitly labeled as preview; reload behavior matches the displayed promise; tests cover both controls.
notes: Discover archive state is now truthful: already-saved items are disabled and follow controls are explicitly labeled as non-durable previews with their limitations disclosed. Covered by UI tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Prevent false collection-share success
description:
## Problem
ShareSheet allows personal/public/community submission when no valid collection exists and reports a generic success while only archiving the item. Require a valid destination, offer a create-collection path, and emit success only after the requested state is accepted.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use an archive with no collection matching the selected personal/public/community destination.
2. Open ShareSheet and select that destination.
3. Submit while the Collection select is empty.
4. Observe the Saved to collection success despite no requested collection assignment.
acceptance_criteria: Collection destinations cannot submit without a valid collection; no success copy names a nonexistent destination; empty-state behavior is explicit; component/integration coverage includes zero-collection and valid-collection paths.
notes: Blocked nonexistent collection submissions, added a create-collection route, validated destinations, and delayed success until archive persistence completes. Covered by ShareSheet interaction tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.
