notes: Three independent read-only reviews completed: interaction/data correctness, accessibility/keyboard, and responsive/product UX. Confirmed: invalid collection success, Discover no-op Save, ephemeral/non-filtering Discover follows, unhandled local persistence failures, silent share/command failures, incomplete modal focus behavior, mobile Settings scroll/safe-area gaps, hidden mobile Commands trigger, landmark/skip-link gaps, undersized controls, and small essential metadata. Partial/stale: remote archive sync now exposes status/offline/retry; Archive grouping/danger treatment has improved; Reader has some view help. Runtime browser verification remains pending because no browser backend was available in this session.

title: Redesign archive library experience
description: Critically improve the archived links and articles UI so the library has stronger editorial hierarchy, clearer navigation and item states, better action prioritization, accessible controls, and robust responsive behavior while preserving archive features.
design: Keep Bareaga's warm editorial visual language, but reduce form-like chrome and establish a calm two-pane library with expressive saved-item cards.
acceptance_criteria: Archive page has a purposeful library header, scannable collection navigation, clear search/filter/sort controls, refined article cards with progressive disclosure for secondary actions, accessible focus/labels, and usable mobile layout. Lint, tests, and build pass.
notes: Rebuilt archive hierarchy and interactions: collection-aware masthead and stats, shelf navigation, contextual filter counts, search clear, three sort modes, prioritized article typography, visible personal notes, progressive disclosure for organization/export, accessible labels/focus targets, and responsive layouts. npm test (62/62), lint, and production build pass. In-app browser was unavailable for screenshot QA.
close_reason: Implemented and validated archive library redesign

title: Fix Maximum update depth loop on app load
description: Starting the Next.js dev server and loading the app repeatedly emits React's 'Maximum update depth exceeded' browser error. Investigate the client state/effect loop in the current UI worktree and prevent repeated state updates on initial render.
acceptance_criteria: Loading /, /discover, and /settings does not emit Maximum update depth errors, and existing interaction behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Stopped the Reader slash-context effect from retriggering Chrome state every render. Stabilized empty feed/custom-source arrays and refresh identity in useFeedQuery; slash context now bails out on unchanged data and only clears on unmount.

title: Make slash command palette + / button global (part of design-system grounding)
description: The slash menu and its / button were reader-only, breaking header parity across pages. Added ChromeProvider (global slash/settings open-state + a slot the Reader registers feed-specific commands into). SiteHeader now renders the / button, Settings button, SlashMenu and SettingsPanel on every page; global , / // ⌘K keyboard handling moved there. slashCommands.ts: reader-only groups (Topics, Articles, refresh/search actions) gated behind an optional reader context; new Navigate group (Go to Reader/Discover/Archive/Social/Product) shown on every page. NewsApp registers its reader context via effect and keeps only r/? shortcuts. Build + lint pass; verified slash menu opens on Reader (with Topics/Articles) and Discover/Archive (reduced) and , opens Settings via keyboard.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in browser

title: Wire custom sources through /api/feeds validation and ranking
description: feedContract.ts:parseFeedQuery hard-rejects any source id not in catalogSourceIds(), and feeds.ts builds its sourceById map only from SOURCE_CATALOG. Both need to also recognize a requesting user's custom sources (resolved from prefs) so /api/feeds doesn't 400 on a legitimately-added custom source, and ranking.ts/getSource() attribution (name, homeUrl) resolves correctly for them.
design: Depends on the data-model task for where custom sources are read from, and on the SSRF-hardening task since this is the code path that actually triggers the network fetch.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting /api/feeds with a custom source id the user has added succeeds and returns articles; requesting an arbitrary unknown id (not in catalog, not a real added custom source) is still rejected exactly as today.
close_reason: Implemented add-source-by-URL UI (Discover + Settings > Sources) backed by a new SSRF-hardened /api/sources/preview endpoint, and wired custom sources through /api/feeds via a new POST path (parseFeedBody, createFeedPostHandler) that re-validates client-supplied sources server-side and never publicly caches.

title: Harden server-side feed fetch against SSRF for user-supplied URLs
description: Today every feedUrl fetched by feeds.ts (parser.parseURL) is a value the project authors hardcoded into sources.ts, so the fetch target is fully trusted. Bring-your-own-feeds means the server will fetch a URL a visitor pastes in, which is a new SSRF risk (e.g. a URL pointing at 169.254.169.254, localhost, or an internal service, including via redirect). Add validation before any fetch of a user-supplied feed URL: enforce https, resolve and reject private/link-local/loopback/multicast IP ranges, re-check the target after following redirects (not just the initial URL), and keep the existing timeout/size caps.
design: This is the one piece of this epic that is a genuine new attack surface, not a UI/data-model extension of existing trusted behavior — treat it as security-critical, not a nice-to-have validation pass.
acceptance_criteria: Attempting to add a source whose feed URL resolves (directly or via redirect) to a private/loopback/link-local address is rejected with a clear error and never reaches parser.parseURL; a normal https Substack/blog feed URL still works.
close_reason: Implemented HTTPS/DNS SSRF validation, redirect revalidation, timeout, and response-size limits.

title: Add custom-source data model and prefs persistence
description: UserPrefs.sourceOrder (src/lib/types.ts) currently only stores IDs that must already exist in the hardcoded SOURCE_CATALOG (src/lib/sources.ts). There is no way to persist a user-supplied feed. Add a customSources: SourceDef[] (or minimal subset: id, name, feedUrl, homeUrl, plus defaulted editorial fields) field to UserPrefs, wire it through prefs.ts load/save/migration, and merge it with SOURCE_CATALOG wherever sources are resolved by id (getSource(), sourceById maps in feeds.ts and ranking.ts).
acceptance_criteria: A custom source added via prefs survives reload, appears in getSource()/sourceById lookups everywhere the catalog is queried, and existing prefs files without the new field still load correctly (backward-compatible migration).
close_reason: Implemented custom source persistence, normalization, ordering, and merged source lookups.

title: Bring-your-own-feeds: import Substack and custom RSS/Atom sources
description: Bareaga's PRD lists bring-your-own-feeds as the immediate roadmap item (docs/PRD.md 'Now' row): let a user paste any RSS/Atom URL (Substack newsletters, personal blogs, any CMS feed) into the existing source manager rather than being limited to the 51 hardcoded catalog sources. The fetch/cache/rank/archive pipeline (src/lib/feeds.ts, ranking.ts) is already source-agnostic RSS/Atom via rss-parser and handles per-source failure isolation; the missing pieces are entirely upstream: no data model for a user-added source, /api/feeds hard-rejects any source id outside the static catalog (src/lib/feedContract.ts), no feed-URL discovery UX, and no SSRF-safe handling for fetching a URL a visitor supplies (today all feedUrls are trusted, hardcoded values).
design: Reuses the existing generic RSS/Atom pipeline (feeds.ts, rss-parser) rather than building a new fetcher. Custom sources get a minimal SourceDef with sensible defaults for the editorial-only fields (sourceType, cadence, depth, defaultRank) so Discover's filters don't break on missing metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A user can paste a Substack (or other blog) URL into Discover or Settings > Sources, Bareaga resolves it to a working RSS/Atom feed (via Substack's /feed convention or HTML <link rel=alternate> autodiscovery), the source appears alongside catalog sources in every existing view (Grid/Top/Focus/Ranked, Archive, Social) with correct name/attribution, persists across reloads via prefs, and the server-side fetch of the user-supplied URL is hardened against SSRF (blocks private/link-local IP ranges and redirects to them, enforces https, caps size/timeout).
close_reason: Completed custom source persistence, SSRF-safe discovery and fetching, private feed API transport, and source management UI with regression coverage.

title: Ground the design system: shared shell across all pages
description: Reader, Discover, Archive, Social, and Product each hand-roll their own header, hero, footer, and button vocabulary in a dedicated stylesheet, with numeric drift (4 wordmark scales, 4 header rhythms, 3 near-duplicate hero blocks, 2 button languages, 2 content widths, missing footers). Extract shared primitives (SiteHeader, PrimaryNav unification, PageHero, SiteFooter, AppShell), add spacing/type/width scale tokens to base.css, put global appearance Settings on every page, unify content width to 1480px, and delete the now-dead per-page CSS.
notes: Done. New shared primitives: AppShell, SiteHeader (wordmark + section label + unified PrimaryNav + global Settings + tools slot + subline), PageHero, SiteFooter. Added layout/spacing/type scale tokens to base.css + new shell.css. PrimaryNav collapsed to one rendering (readerStyle removed); all pages show all links with aria-current underline; Archive count badge shows app-wide. Settings (theme/palette/font/density) now reachable on every page, opens to Appearance tab on non-reader pages. Cross-cutting chrome via window 'bareaga:chrome' CustomEvent (, shortcut + slash-menu 'open settings'). Product moved onto shared header + 1480px width (dropped 1240px + double-padding), kept its editorial hero/feature-grid/manifesto/CTA-footer, added .product-subnav. Deleted dead per-page CSS from reader/discover/archive-social/product/responsive. Build + lint pass. Verified all 5 pages + Settings-on-archive in browser.
close_reason: Closed

title: Create shared app shell and browser data stores
description: Centralize theme hydration, shared navigation, preference state, and archive state behind reusable providers/hooks and repository interfaces. Separate archive domain operations, seeded demo fixtures, validation/migrations, and localStorage implementation so synced storage can replace persistence without rewriting screens.
acceptance_criteria: Reader, Discover, Archive, and Social use one theme/prefs integration; archive mutations go through a typed repository with runtime validation and migration tests; page shells share navigation primitives; the existing synced archive feature can depend on the repository rather than UI-local storage functions.
close_reason: Centralized preference/theme and archive state in root providers; introduced typed archive repository, localStorage adapter, fixtures, domain operations, runtime validation and migrations; moved Reader, Discover, Archive, Social, and ShareSheet off direct persistence; added shared primary navigation and migration/repository tests. 30 tests, TypeScript, lint aside from tracked font warning, and build pass.

title: Harden feed API and isolate server-only modules
description: Define a validated feed-query contract, deduplicate and reject unknown inputs, protect or rate-limit force refresh before deployment, make cache semantics explicit, and split server-only RSS/provider enrichment from browser-safe engagement formatting with server-only guards.
acceptance_criteria: The public route validates and deduplicates ids/topics, abusive refresh requests cannot repeatedly fan out to publishers, server-only code cannot enter client module graphs, and route/cache behavior has automated tests.
close_reason: Validated and deduplicated feed query contract; rejected unknown inputs; added bounded per-client forced-refresh budget; made cache headers explicit; isolated RSS/provider code with server-only guards; added route, cache, validation, and limiter tests. Tests, TypeScript, lint, and build pass.

title: Extract and harden reader feed orchestration
description: Move feed request/cache/abort/progressive-refresh state out of NewsApp into a focused query hook or service with an explicit state model. Preserve cached sources during revalidation, use bounded parallel batches or justify sequential behavior, tolerate per-batch failures, and reduce NewsApp to composition and user intents.
acceptance_criteria: Cached sources do not disappear during background refresh; batch failures do not prevent unrelated sources from loading; cancellation, topic changes, retry, and force refresh have automated coverage; NewsApp no longer owns transport/cache mechanics.
close_reason: Extracted reader transport/cache/cancellation into useFeedQuery and a bounded-concurrency feed orchestrator; preserved cached sources during revalidation; isolated batch failures; added cancellation, topic, retry, force-refresh, merge, and concurrency tests. Tests, TypeScript, production build, and lint (aside from the existing font warning) verified.

title: Preserve removed sources during preference merge
description: The legacy merge path appends every starter source to sourceOrder, which undoes Discover removals after reload. Treat an explicitly stored sourceOrder, including an empty array, as the user's enabled set while still defaulting when the property is absent.
acceptance_criteria: Removing starter sources or all sources persists after LocalPrefsStore reload; missing sourceOrder still receives the starter defaults.
close_reason: Updated preference merging to preserve explicit enabled-source sets, including empty sets, added regression coverage, and verified removal persistence across a live reload.

title: Build Discover Sources MVP
description: Split the built-in source catalog from the default enabled set, enrich source metadata with topics and tags, add a /discover browsing and search experience, and let users locally add or remove catalog sources while preserving the current starter set.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated Discover nav/page supports search, category and metadata filters, source preview cards, and persistent add/remove actions. Existing users retain the current starter sources by default. Tests, lint, typecheck, and build pass.
close_reason: Implemented the local-first Discover Sources MVP with a 51-feed catalog, preserved starter set, discovery filters and sorting, persistent add/remove and private ratings, responsive UI, and regression coverage.

title: Add Obsidian and Notion archive interoperability
description: Make Bareaga archives portable into existing knowledge systems through open Markdown with frontmatter, CSV, copyable citation/clip formats, and documented import affordances; preserve source URL, authorship, notes, tags, collection, and timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Users can export an archive or collection to Obsidian-friendly Markdown and Notion-friendly CSV/Markdown without losing URLs, notes, tags, collection context, or saved dates.
close_reason: Implemented Obsidian-friendly Markdown with frontmatter, Notion-friendly CSV, per-item copyable Markdown, archive/collection export controls, and export preservation tests.

title: Add synced archival storage and durable snapshots
description: Move the local-first archive behind a synced storage interface so saves, notes, tags, and collections travel across devices; add optional content snapshots and export/import while preserving canonical URLs and source context.
design: Optional Supabase passwordless auth; Postgres immutable archive revisions and idempotent operations; private Storage for captured content; same-origin Next.js authenticated APIs; sync v1 uses server revisions and field-level optimistic conflict detection, with explicit server-wins conflicts for same-field and delete/update races.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated archives sync across devices, save metadata remains portable, and users can export their data without losing canonical source context.
notes: Foundation slice completed in bareaga_web-6j1.1. Remaining implementation is sequenced as 6j1.2 authenticated APIs, 6j1.3 local-first client sync/migration, then 6j1.4 snapshots/export/recovery/account controls. Keep parent open until cross-device acceptance criteria pass.
close_reason: All subtasks (6j1.1-6j1.5) complete. Cross-device authenticated sync, portable metadata, and lossless export are implemented and validated end-to-end: pgTAP passes, and a live smoke test against the running Supabase stack confirmed real Auth signup, PostgREST RLS scoping across archives/archive_revisions/content_snapshots, and private Storage bucket access control all behave correctly.

title: Build archive, collections, and archive search experience
description: Expand Bareaga beyond RSS reading with a first archival product slice: saved-item states, collections, archive-native search/filtering, and a credible shared/social collection concept that fits the existing editorial UI.
acceptance_criteria: Users can navigate to an Archive surface, search and filter saved material, change meaningful archival states, create collections, and see how collections can be shared; state persists locally and the existing reader still builds.
close_reason: Implemented reader-to-archive saving, persistent archive states, notes, search, filters, collections, collection creation and sharing intent; build and tests pass.

title: Implement reader UX hierarchy and mobile ergonomics
description: Apply the attached UX audit to the Bareaga reader and product surfaces, prioritizing truthful loading state, entity decoding, mobile progressive disclosure, clearer reading modes, settings hierarchy, story scanability, and accessibility.
acceptance_criteria: Reader reports configured/loaded/failed sources accurately; encoded feed titles render correctly; mobile toolbar exposes stories sooner; reading modes are explained; settings and story hierarchy are improved; product page is rebalanced; relevant checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented the UX audit priorities: truthful progressive status, entity decoding, mobile progressive disclosure, mode explanations, settings tabs and source search, story hierarchy/accessibility improvements, return bar, and a shorter product page. Lint and production build pass.

title: Add transparent personalized article ranking
description: Implement a Ranked home view with weighted keyword rules, per-source preferences, recency and normalized engagement scoring, diversity adjustments, visible score explanations, keyword highlighting, persisted settings controls, and automated tests.
close_reason: Implemented transparent personalized ranking, persisted keyword/source preferences, UI controls, score explanations, highlighting, diversity, tests, and production/browser verification.

title: Restore Grid as a third reading view
description: Bring back the original source-column Grid alongside Top and Focus, preserving column controls, drag reordering, source-level errors, and per-source retry without regressing the new accessibility and transition guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Grid, Top, and Focus are all selectable with accessible selected-state semantics; legacy Grid preferences remain Grid; Grid supports configured columns, drag reordering, source details, and retry; lint and build pass.
close_reason: Restored Grid as a first-class third view with original column controls, drag ordering, detail options, and source retry; lint and production build pass.

title: Rework feed views and accessibility contracts
description: Implement the requested Settings accessibility behavior, transition consistency, selected-state semantics and touch targets, recency-based Focus, deterministic balanced Top, clearer loading/import/feed errors, and simpler keyboard/settings UI.
acceptance_criteria: Settings has a truthful accessible interaction contract; topic label/content cannot disagree; selections expose semantics with adequate targets; Focus is globally recency-sorted with Compact/Detailed modes; Top is deterministic and transparently balanced; loading and errors are human-readable; keyboard help and Settings are simplified; quality gates pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified; lint has no errors and the production build passes.

title: Synthesis pass
description: Update docs/codebase-findings.md with confirmed findings (F-31+). Final writer of the catalog.
acceptance_criteria: codebase-findings.md updated.
close_reason: Pass 5 synthesis: catalog F-31–F-51 assigned; F-01–F-30 updated in place (fixed-on-tree / narrowed / merges); launch beads dcr.2 (F-31) and dcr.3 (F-32); vendor beads w3p/kbt/m31 notes retargeted to problems; bd remember codebase-findings refreshed. Parent dcr left OPEN. No commit.

description: Independent review of slice findings for consistency and evidence quality.

notes:
# Skeptic pass — bareaga_web-dcr.1.12
Date: 2026-09-11. Independent file opens against S1–S10 notes + catalog F-01–F-30. No findings.md edit, no implementation beads, no product code, no commit.

Method: every F-TEMP citation opened; F-xx slice verdicts re-checked on tree. Kill rules: wrong citation → reject; already F-01–F-30 → merge; fixed-on-tree (dmm/jc1/ky6/l4v/thread_root_key) → mark; launch only if a 5k archive / first Notion connect / popular profile would hit it; missing evidence → reject or demote, not keep-as-launch; vendor-shaped → reject (none were).

Contrast: `readQueue` preserves `coeus.archive.sync-queue.v1.corrupt`. Disk is **not** overwritten on parse fail (`valid && migrated` guard). Data loss needs a subsequent `save`. localStorage `setItem` is typically atomic — truncated-write as first-user path is unshown. Falsifiable: corrupt-key copy like the queue.

### Slice S10 — Cross-cutting platform + Next 16.3
Date: 2026-09-10. Files: next.config.ts, src/proxy.ts, vercel.json, src/lib/securityHeaders.ts, src/app/robots.ts, src/app/sitemap.ts.
Next claims checked against installed next@16.3.4 docs under node_modules/next/dist/docs (proxy, after, cookies, robots, sitemap, headers, rewrites, maxDuration, CSP, streaming, authentication optimistic checks, proxyClientMaxBodySize). Platform §7.4 cited from memory `vercel-supabase-platform-limits` (not re-invented).

Runtime flow:
1. Incoming request: next.config `headers()` (`/:path*` → `securityHeaders(NODE_ENV==="production")`) then next.config redirects (none) then `src/proxy.ts` `proxy()` then filesystem then afterFiles rewrites (`/@:handle*` → `/u/:handle*`). Docs: proxy.md execution order; rewrites.md afterFiles = array return.
2. Proxy (named export `proxy`, Node runtime default in v16.0.0): skip if Supabase URL/key missing; else `@supabase/ssr` `createServerClient` + `auth.getClaims()` (JWT, no DB). `decideProxyRedirect(pathname, signedIn)` only special-cases `/welcome` and `/signin`. Matcher skips `api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|image ext` — API cron is not proxied.
3. Cron: vercel.json `crons[0]` GET `/api/archive/destinations/worker` schedule `0 6 * * *`. Worker `GET` checks `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET` (S2 pointer).
4. Metadata: `robots.ts` / `sitemap.ts` `MetadataRoute.*`; origin = `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000"`. Sitemap enumerates seven marketing/app shells, not profiles/collections.

Re-verification table:
| F-xx | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| F-02 | **cron claim stands**; catalog maxDuration/lease text is **stale** (S2) | `vercel.json` still one cron `path: /api/archive/destinations/worker` `schedule: 0 6 * * *`. Memory: Hobby cron min = once/day (sub-daily fails at deploy). `after()` duration = route maxDuration; platform default maxDuration 300s all plans. Catalog "only cron route sets maxDuration=300" is false on this tree: `export const maxDuration = 300` on `src/app/api/archive/destinations/worker/route.ts`, `.../sync/route.ts`, and `.../destinations/[destinationId]/sync/route.ts` (outside this slice). Catalog `leaseTtlSeconds` default 120 is also stale: `destinationWorker.server.ts` `leaseTtlSeconds ?? 300`. Closed beads `bareaga_web-ky6` / `bareaga_web-l4v`. Remaining F-02 risk is dispatch/chunking/Hobby daily catch-up, not "cron more often" on Hobby. |
| F-03 | **stands** (body cap still not encoded in platform config) | Neither `next.config.ts` nor `vercel.json` sets a 4.5 MB cap (`proxyClientMaxBodySize` unset — Next 16.3 default 10MB and only applies when proxy runs; matcher excludes `api`). Memory: Vercel request **and** response body hard cap 4.5 MB → 413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE unless streamed. Pointer S1/F-03: `archiveApi.ts` `handleArchiveGet` still `Response.json(archive)` (not a `ReadableStream`). Do not mint a new F-id. |
| F-20 | **CSP `img-src https:` claim is stale / fixed-on-tree**; upload-path half is out of slice | `securityHeaders.ts` `supabaseImgSources` + `imgSrc` = `'self' data: blob: https://*.supabase.co` + configured origin. Unit `securityHeaders.test.mjs` asserts `doesNotMatch(csp, /img-src[^;]*\bhttps:(?!\/\/)/)`. Comment names F-20/F-25. Residual: wildcard `https://*.supabase.co` is still any Supabase project, not only `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` (defence-in-depth vs F-25 host pin). `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` still present; Next 16.3 CSP guide wants a per-request nonce in **proxy** (`content-security-policy.md`); `next.config` `headers()` is static so cannot nonce. `frame-src https:` still unbounded (comment: reader previews). |
| F-21 | **stands**; §7.13 still a product call | `robots.ts` `disallow` includes `"/u/"` not `/@`. `next.config.ts` `rewrites()` maps `/@:handle` → `/u/:handle` at afterFiles, so a crawler of `/@alice` sees profile HTML with URL still `/@alice`. `sitemap.ts` does not enumerate profiles (comment: unbounded DB crawl). Pointer S4: `src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx` `generateMetadata` sets `alternates.canonical: /@${handle}` and **no** `robots.index` (unlike `src/app/c/[slug]/page.tsx`). |

§7.4 Vercel limits (memory `vercel-supabase-platform-limits`, 2026-09-09): default maxDuration 300s Hobby+Pro; after() = route max duration via Fluid waitUntil; req+resp body 4.5 MB unless streamed (Node streaming needs no config); Hobby cron once/day only. Installed `maxDuration.md`: option is a number, default "set by deployment platform". Installed `after.md`: after() in Route Handlers may call `cookies()`/`headers()`; in Server Components must not. Proxy may use `after()`; this `proxy.ts` does not.

### Slice S7 — Client hot path + UI orchestration

Date: 2026-09-11. Tree re-read of listed files plus SiteHeader/ChromeProvider/slashCommands (F-09/F-11 evidence lives there; AppShell only re-exports them).

Runtime flow:

1. `src/app/layout.tsx` RootLayout wraps every route in AppProviders (Auth → Preferences → Archive → Chrome). Five `next/font/google` families on `<html>`.
2. `usePreferencesProvider` hydrates `coeus.prefs.v1`, writes `data-theme|palette|font|density|homeView|storyRepresentation` on `<html>`, debounces `prefsStore.save` 200ms after the first non-hydrate prefs identity.
3. `useArchiveProvider` hydrates `SyncedArchiveRepository`, owns `PersistenceQueue`, publishes archive + persistence + sync on the root context. `updateArchive` clones via the caller, `setArchive(next)`, `queue.enqueue(next)`.
4. `AppShell` renders `SiteHeader` + children + `SiteFooter`. Header consumes both contexts (prefs, full archive for nav count + persistence banner).
5. Reader (`src/app/page.tsx` → NewsApp): `useFeedQuery` batches; `SearchBar` is controlled; `onSearchChange` writes `lastSearch` into prefs every keystroke; `useDeferredValue` only delays `filterSources` / match counts; slash registration writes `currentSources` into ChromeProvider with a reference-equality guard.
6. Archive (`ArchiveApp` is an 89-line shell): `useArchiveFilters` computes `visible`; `ArchiveList` mounts `visible.slice(0, renderLimit)` (100, then +100); `ArchiveSidebar` counts per collection.

Remaining: list is still document-scrolled, variable-height (`<details>` notes/tools), no `content-visibility` on `.archive-item` (contrast `.source-col` in `reader.css`). Clicking through "show more" can still mount the 5,000 ceiling. Sidebar `itemCountIn` is still `data.items.filter(...includes(id)).length` per collection per render (`ArchiveSidebar`, budget 2,000 × 5,000). `bareaga_web-w3p` names a library; the remaining problem is still unbounded-if-paged DOM + O(C×N) sidebar counts + per-card collection `<option>`s (F-TEMP-S7-2). ### Slice S6 — Conversations + social graph reads

Date: 2026-09-10. Tree re-read; no findings.md edits; no product code.

Runtime flow:

Writes (BFF + admin client + security-definer RPCs):
1. POST /api/likes|reposts|replies (src/app/api/{likes,reposts,replies}/route.ts) → conversationApi.handle* → authenticateArchiveRequest.
2. parseTargetRefRequest / parseCreateReplyRequest (conversation.ts).
3. gateTarget: store.resolveTarget + actorFollows + actorCanReachTarget (canSee toward TARGET owner). 404 missing/unpublished collection; 403 cannot see. Unlisted is reachable (link).
4. RPC like_target / repost_target / create_reply (conversationStore.server.ts). create_reply inherits the target's current visibility; parent must share (target_type, target_id).
5. DELETE /api/likes|reposts and DELETE /api/replies/[id] skip the can-see gate (retract own row). PATCH update_reply is author-scoped.
6. /social (src/app/social/page.tsx) is only permanentRedirect("/discover").

Reads:
1. Profile Replies/Likes/Reposts tabs (S4 page): SupabaseConversationProfileReader.listRepliesByActor / listLikesByActor / listRepostsByActor + followsAmong + threadDescendantCounts → deriveReplyThreads / deriveInteractionFeed (conversationProfile.ts). Caps: REPLY_ROOT_LIMIT=50, INTERACTION_LIMIT=100, REPLY_DESCENDANT_LIMIT=200 per childrenOf hop, two hops.
2. Dedicated thread page (threadPageLoader.server.ts, outside glob but sole loadThreadPage caller): RPC thread_descendants keyset (THREAD_PAGE_SIZE=40, RPC clamp 200) → deriveThreadView.
3. Discover Following: src/app/discover/page.tsx (caller outside glob) → SupabaseFollowedFeedReader.listFollowedPeopleContent → combineFollowedFeed (visibility + offset page). PAGE_SIZE=20. engagement* is not imported from this glob (HN metrics live in S3).

2. Owner publishes a post: POST /api/posts/publish → `archiveItem()` same full-snapshot select, `derivePostSnapshot` / `parsePostSnapshot`, RPC `publish_post`.
3. Public listing: GET /c and GET /api/collections/discover → `listPublic` (`visibility='public'` AND live).
4. Direct link: GET /c/[slug] → `getBySlug` (any live tier, admin client) then `canReadPublication` → `canSee`. RSS `/c/[slug]/rss.xml` keeps public/unlisted only.
5. Owner list: GET /api/collections → `list(ownerId)` via archive_id. GET /api/posts → `listByAuthor(userId)` (self).

Solid, tested, do not replace:

- `validatedHttpsUrl`: https, no user/password, `isIP` literal or `dnsLookup({all:true,verbatim:true})`, **any** unsafe address → throw.
- Decimal/octal/hex IPv4 in URLs: WHATWG normalizes (`https://2130706433/` → `127.0.0.1`) then `ipv4IsUnsafe` — blocked (probed).
- Pin: `fixedAddressLookup` supports `{all:true}` (memory `feed-fetch-lookup-hook-needs-all-option`) **and** legacy callback. Tested.

- `fetchHnItemEngagement` uses global `fetch` to a hardcoded Firebase URL (not user-controlled).
- Refresh/preview budgets are process-local (HANDOFF known boundary).

- **who_hurts:** Hobby function-time/memory; publishers at the other end of attacker-supplied public URLs.
- **what_would_falsify_it:** a platform/WAF rate limit in front of `/api/feeds`; or a missed app-level limiter on the miss path.

- **related_beads:** F-16, HANDOFF process-local cache/limiter
- **needs_measurement:** miss QPS and function duration on a public deploy.

### F-TEMP-S3-2
- **title:** Dotted IPv4-mapped AAAA answers are classified unsafe (including public)
- **tag:** later (availability, fail-closed)
- **confidence:** confirmed for `isUnsafeIp`; **inferred** that Node `dns.lookup` ever returns this form

- **who_hurts:** readers of a host whose resolver synthesizes dotted-mapped AAAA (unusual).
- **what_would_falsify_it:** Node 24 `dns.lookup({all:true})` never returns dotted-mapped forms in production.

# S2 Destinations + durable dispatch (pass 5)

Slice files only. Evidence is current working tree. Do not treat Inngest/Queues as findings.

## Runtime flow (connect → lease → tick → adapter → prune)

1. **Connect**
   - Obsidian: `POST /api/archive/destinations` → `handleConnectDestination` → `SupabaseDestinationsStore.connect` → RPC `create_destination` (AES-256-GCM secret). Unique `(archive_id, kind)`.
   - Notion: `GET .../notion/oauth/start` → signed nonce in `notion_oauth_states` → Notion authorize → `GET .../oauth/callback` → token exchange + `POST /v1/search` (first database only) → `store.connect("notion", ...)`.
   - Neither connect path calls `runDestinationWorkerTick`. UI (`DestinationsPanel`) notifies "connected" and reloads; user must click **Sync now** (`POST .../[kind]/sync`), wait for the next archive `POST /api/archive/sync` `after()` hook, or wait for daily cron.

2. **Triggers (three, overlapping)**
   - Primary: `src/app/api/archive/sync/route.ts` `after()` with `ownerId` captured *before* `after()` (F-27 fix). `maxDuration = 300`. Skips if `DESTINATION_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` missing or `ownerId` null.
   - Manual: `src/app/api/archive/destinations/[destinationId]/sync/route.ts` `maxDuration = 300`, `minIntervalSeconds: 0` (lease still exclusive).
   - Catch-up: `GET /api/archive/destinations/worker` Bearer `CRON_SECRET`, `vercel.json` `0 6 * * *`, `maxDuration = 300`. Hobby once/day. Also runs `sweep_conversation_orphans` + `prune_all_archive_revisions` (not destination-attempt prune).

3. **Lease**
   - `runDestinationWorkerTick` default `leaseTtlSeconds = 300`, `minIntervalSeconds = 30`.
   - `acquire_destination_delivery_lease`: atomic UPDATE; deny if not `active`, live lease, or `delivery_started_at` inside min interval.
   - `release_destination_delivery_lease`: no-op on stale token (no clobber).
   - pgTAP still passes TTL **120** as a test argument (`destination_delivery_lease.test.sql`); that is not the worker default.

4. **Tick**
   - `activeDestinations(ownerId?)` via `readAllPages` (page 1000). Decrypts secrets in process.
   - Per target: acquire → `runDeliveryForDestination` → `recordOutcomes` (one RPC `record_delivery_outcomes`) → `markStatus(auth_error)` if needed → release.
   - `MAX_ITEMS_PER_TICK = 100` (`destinationWorker.server.ts`). Dirty set from `computeDirtyItems(snapshot, deliveries)`.
   - Never throws out of the tick; per-destination failures go to `results`/`failures`.

5. **Adapters**
   - Notion: sequential `runDestinationDelivery` → `NotionAdapter.pushUpsert/pushDelete`. Create = POST page + one paragraph block; update = PATCH **title properties only**; delete = `archived: true`. Stop batch on first `authError`. `fetchWithRetry` (timeout 10s, retries 2, Retry-After clamped 120s).
   - Obsidian/GitHub: `GitHubGitAdapter.pushBatch` with `GITHUB_TREE_CHUNK_SIZE = 500` and `base_tree`; worker already slices to 100 so production is one chunk/tick. 5 Git Data API calls per chunk (ref, commit, tree, commit, PATCH ref). Failed chunk fails that chunk all-or-nothing; earlier successful chunks stay watermarked; remainder mapped retryable without further writes.

6. **Prune**
   - Disconnect: secret cleared, status `disabled`, watermarks kept (reconnect will not recreate `external_ref`s).
   - Purge: row delete cascades to `destination_deliveries` and `destination_delivery_attempts`.
   - `destination_delivery_attempts` is append-only; cron does **not** prune it. UI reads `destination_deliveries`, not attempts.

`shareDestination.ts` is ShareSheet collection routing, not Notion/Obsidian/GitHub outbound. Naming collision only.

Other catalog reads (follows, collections, recovery) not in this slice. Catalog table still lists `destinationsStore.server.ts` `deliveries()` / `activeDestinations()` as unbounded — **stale**. |

Cap **100**. GitHub chunk **500** + `base_tree`. Batch `record_delivery_outcomes`. `maxDuration = 300` on sync, manual sync, and cron. `after()` captures `ownerId` (no cookie re-auth). Hobby cron still `0 6 * * *`. after() still primary near-real-time trigger. Connect/OAuth still do not start a tick. 5000-item archive still needs 50 successful ticks; if only cron fires, 50 days. Attempts still unpruned. Sequential Notion still. Duplicate-page risk from lease TTL < run time **largely removed** (TTL=budget and 100-item cap). | **Partially fixed. Launch tag remains for start/finish, not for the 120-vs-300 lease mismatch.** Catalog bullets about 120s lease, missing maxDuration, per-item RPC, unchunked GitHub, after() re-auth are **stale**. |

It does not read `status`. `record_delivery_outcomes` inserts failed rows with `last_delivered_revision = 0` and on conflict does not advance it. First-connect of items whose `fieldRevision` is 0 (explicitly supported: comment + test “newly connected destination is dirty … even at revision 0”) leaves a delivery row at revision 0 after `failed_retryable`; next tick sees `0 > 0` false and skips. No unit test covers failed-then-retry at revision 0. Production `initialize_archive` uses `EMPTY_ARCHIVE`; items added via `applyArchiveSyncBatch` typically have max field revision ≥ 1, so those *do* retry (`1 > 0`). Disconnect/reconnect preserves watermarks, so a rev-0 failure stays suppressed after reconnect unless `?purge=1`.
- **who_hurts:** First-connect of never-edited (field-revision 0) items that hit a transient GitHub/Notion error; demo/test snapshots; any future path that lands items in the initial snapshot at revision 0.
- **what_would_falsify_it:** Dirty check also treats `status !== "delivered"` as dirty; or production never has fieldRevision 0 items (does not erase the comparator hole).
- **suggested_shape:** Dirty if no delivery, or `status` in `{failed_retryable, failed_auth, pending}`, or `revision > lastDeliveredRevision`. Add a delivery test: fail upsert at rev 0 → still dirty.
- **related_beads:** F-02 (retry/dispatch); `bareaga_web-m31` is not the fix

### Slice S1 — Archive + sync + persistence

Runtime flow:
1. User stars/notes on /archive (ArchiveApp) or reader → `useArchiveProvider.updateArchive`.
2. Optimistic React state; `PersistenceQueue.enqueue(next)` → `SyncedArchiveRepository.save`.
3. `local.save` → `migrateArchiveData` + `JSON.stringify` into `coeus.archive.v1`.
4. `operationsForChange(before, after)` diffs every field of every entity via `JSON.stringify`; pending ops appended to `coeus.archive.sync-queue.v1`.
5. `synchronize()` GET `/api/archive` (`handleArchiveGet` → `store.getOrCreate` selects full current JSONB snapshot).
6. POST `/api/archive/sync` (`handleArchiveSync`): 2 MiB body cap, rate-limit RPC, `applyArchiveSyncBatch`, `checkArchiveBudget`, `commit_archive_sync` CAS; response is the new full snapshot (`Response.json`).
7. Client rebases leftover ops, `local.save` again. Sync route `after()` kicks destination worker (S2).
8. Recovery/export: `handleArchiveExport` / revisions / restore / content capture under `/api/archive/{export,revisions,snapshots}`.

| F-xx | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| F-03 | stands (pass-4 numbers still exact) | `ARCHIVE_BUDGET.maxSnapshotBytes = 8 * 1024 * 1024` (`archiveBudget.ts`). `MAX_SYNC_BODY_BYTES = 2 * 1024 * 1024` (`archiveApi.ts`). GET `/api/archive` is still `Response.json(archive)` with no stream (`archiveApi.ts` `handleArchiveGet`; `src/app/api/archive/route.ts` has no `maxDuration`, no streaming). Sync POST sets `maxDuration = 300` (`sync/route.ts`). Any `getOrCreate` throw → 503 (`handleArchiveGet` catch-all). Platform 4.5 MB req+resp still from `vercel-supabase-platform-limits` memory, not encoded in app. |
| F-05 | narrowed / partially fixed-on-tree | Catalog text is stale. `persistenceQueue.test.mjs` now asserts coalescing: sync enqueues save only `[3]`; in-flight save + two more saves `[1, 3]`. `enqueue` always writes `this.pending = { value, version }` so later values replace the pending snapshot (`persistenceQueue.ts`). Remaining cost: each *actual* `repository.save` still runs full `migrateArchiveData` (`new URL` per item in `archiveValidation.ts`) + `JSON.stringify` of the whole archive + `operationsForChange` which `JSON.stringify`s every field of every entity (`syncedArchiveRepository.ts`). Queue persist is a second full `JSON.stringify(this.queue)`. |
| F-07 | fixed-on-tree (SQL + pgTAP); catalog/comments stale | Closed bead `bareaga_web-jc1`. Migration `20260909170000_cap_archive_revision_retention.sql` replaces AND with OR: delete when `revision <= cutoff OR created_at < now()-keepDays`, never the current revision. pgTAP `archive_quotas_retention.test.sql` asserts count-window prune of *new* extra revisions (4 deleted, 2 kept) and age prune inside the count window (old rev 4 deleted). title: Table lockdown migration never revokes EXECUTE on public functions (F-29)
description: 20260907100000_lock_down_public_tables.sql revokes ALL ON ALL TABLES from anon/authenticated and sets ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for TABLES, but never touches functions. Postgres grants EXECUTE on a new function to PUBLIC; PostgREST exposes public-schema functions as POST /rest/v1/rpc/<name> to the request role. title: archive sync after() hook re-reads cookies instead of capturing ownerId (F-27)
description: src/app/api/archive/sync/route.ts: handleArchiveSync authenticates the request, then after() calls authenticateArchiveRequest() AGAIN -> createRequestSupabaseClient -> cookies() -> getClaims(); createRequestSupabaseClient.setAll writes cookies. Per installed next/dist/docs/.../after.md, route handlers CAN read cookies in after() (won't throw), so delivery is not silently skipped — but (1) redundant getClaims per sync, (2) if getClaims triggers a Supabase token refresh, the rotated Set-Cookie is emitted after the response is flushed and dropped -> browser's refresh token goes stale -> intermittent forced sign-out / refresh-reuse lockout. design: Capture ownerId once in the route before after() (single authenticateArchiveRequest() call; pass 'authenticate: async () => ownerId' into handleArchiveSync). Inside after(), use the cookie-free admin client only; never call authenticateArchiveRequest().

close_reason: sync/route.ts now calls authenticateArchiveRequest() once before after() and passes 'authenticate: async () => ownerId' to handleArchiveSync; the after() hook reuses the captured ownerId and never calls cookies()/getClaims() again. tsc + lint + 478 unit green. title: Allow handle edit in the profile API + rate limit and squatting guard
description:
Drop handle immutability from the profile save path, and add the two guards that make it safe: a rate limit on how often an account can change handle, and the quarantine check from task 4.1 at claim time.

validateProfileInput is UNCHANGED - the handle shape rule never varies. What changes is the store: saving a profile whose handle differs from the stored one now releases the old handle into handle_history within the same transaction.
design:
In src/lib/profileStore.server.ts, save() gains the release step. Because it must be atomic with the profiles update, this needs a security-definer RPC (change_handle) rather than two client calls - follow the publish_collection pattern including the revoke/grant to service_role.

Claim-time checks, in order:
1. The shape check (already in validateProfileInput).
2. Not currently held in profiles - the existing unique constraint, surfacing as HandleTakenError and a 409, unchanged.
3. Not in handle_history within the quarantine window, unless the requester is the original owner. A new typed error - HandleQuarantinedError - mapping to a 409 with a distinct message, since "taken" and "recently released by someone else" are different situations for the user.
4. Rate limit: at most N changes per account per rolling year, counted from handle_history. src/lib/fixedWindowBudget.ts already exists in this codebase - check whether it fits before writing a new limiter.

Update WelcomeForm.tsx copy if it currently implies the handle is permanent.
acceptance_criteria:
- An onboarded account can change its handle.
- The old handle is released into handle_history atomically with the update.
- A handle held by another account returns 409 with field handle, as today.
- A quarantined handle returns 409 with a distinct message.
- Exceeding the rate limit returns 429 with the time the next change is allowed.
- profileApi tests cover the taken, quarantined and rate-limited paths.
close_reason: save() routes a changed handle through change_handle RPC; rolling-year rate limit (3/yr) from handle_history; HandleQuarantinedError->409 distinct msg, HandleChangeRateLimitedError->429 Retry-After; WelcomeForm copy + 429 handling; profileApi tests for taken/quarantined/rate-limited

title: Migration: handle_history + quarantine window
description: Record every handle a profile has released, so old links keep resolving and a released handle cannot be immediately reclaimed by someone else.
acceptance_criteria:
- Table and index exist; old_handle enforces the same shape as profiles.handle.
- A third party cannot claim a handle released fewer than 30 days ago.
- The original owner can reclaim their own released handle immediately.
- Release plus profile update is atomic.
- pgTAP covers the quarantine rule and the original-owner exemption.

title: resolveHandle returns redirectFrom; the page issues a permanent redirect
description:
Fill in the seam Phase 1 left. resolveHandle() looks up handle_history when the handle is not found in profiles, and returns the current profile with redirectFrom set to the retired handle. The page then issues a permanentRedirect() to the canonical /@handle.

Because every handle lookup already goes through resolveHandle, this is a change to one function and a three-line addition to the page.
design:
In src/lib/profileStore.server.ts resolveHandle becomes:
1. select from profiles by handle - hit means { profile, redirectFrom: null }.
2. miss: select from handle_history by old_handle, joining profiles - hit means { profile, redirectFrom: <old handle> }.
3. miss again means null, which the page turns into notFound().

In src/app/u/[handle]/page.tsx, after the load: if redirectFrom is set, call permanentRedirect(`/@${profile.handle}`). A 308 rather than a 307, since the move is permanent and search engines should follow it.

Check the Next docs at node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/permanentRedirect.md before relying on the exact semantics in this version - redirect() and permanentRedirect() throw, so they must be called outside a try block.

Do the same in generateMetadata, or accept that the metadata for a redirecting request is discarded anyway - confirm which and note it.

Extend the followers and following routes from task 2.11 identically if they have landed.
acceptance_criteria:
- A request to a retired handle 308s to the current handle.
- A request to a never-existing handle still 404s.
- Two hops never occur: a retired handle always redirects straight to the current one, not through an intermediate.
- The redirect fires before any rendering work.
close_reason: resolveHandle falls back to handle_history and resolves the profile by id (no redirect chains); /@handle + followers + following pages 308 to canonical before any render

title: [Parallel] Handle changes with redirects
description:
Let someone change their handle after onboarding, without breaking every link that pointed at the old one.

Not on the Phase 1 to 2 to 3 critical path - it can land any time after Phase 1 - but Phase 1 has to BUILD FOR IT. That is the entire reason task 1.7 routes every handle lookup through resolveHandle(): the history lookup slots in behind that one function without touching the page.

Doing this properly needs three things beyond dropping the immutability: a history table so old links still resolve, a quarantine window so a released handle cannot be immediately grabbed by an impersonator, and a rate limit so handles cannot be cycled to squat.
design: resolveHandle already returns { profile, redirectFrom }. In Phase 1 redirectFrom is always null; this sub-epic fills it from handle_history and the page issues a permanentRedirect() when it is set.
acceptance_criteria:
- A handle can be changed, subject to the rate limit.
- A link to a retired handle 301s to the current one.
- A released handle cannot be claimed by another account inside the quarantine window.
- Nothing in the profile page itself changes beyond honouring redirectFrom.
close_reason: All 3 children shipped: handle_history migration + quarantine + atomic change_handle, resolveHandle redirect fallback, profile API handle-edit with rate limit and squatting guard

title: UI: Replies tab + two-level thread rendering
description:
The Replies tab and the threaded view. Renders a top-level reply with the object it replies to as context, then its direct responses indented one level. Anything deeper flattens into that second level with a replying-to prefix naming the parent author.

This is a rendering decision, not a schema one - parent_id supports arbitrary depth and the plan deliberately caps the DISPLAY so the query stays one bounded fetch and the layout survives a narrow viewport.
design:
Query: fetch top-level replies for this author (parent_id is null) with their targets, then one further fetch for all direct children of that page of replies. Two queries, bounded, no recursive CTE.

Flattening: a reply whose parent is itself a child renders at the second level with "replying to @handle" as its lead. Determine this from the parent chain in the fetched set; if the grandparent is outside the page, still render at level two - correctness of position matters more than completeness of context here.

Indentation: one level only, via a left rule and padding, per the mockup reply-nested treatment. At 320px the indent must not push the body under about 40 characters - test it.

The reply composer is a client island; keep it small and reuse the visibility control component from task 2.10.
acceptance_criteria:
- Top-level replies render with their target as context.
- Direct responses render indented one level.
- A third-level reply renders at level two with a replying-to prefix.
- No horizontal scroll or sub-40-character measure at 320px.
- The composer defaults its visibility to the target visibility.

ProfileReplies.tsx (client, router.refresh on post), ReplyComposer.tsx island reusing VisibilitySelect read-only seeded to the inherited target tier. Owner-only replyComposeTargets sibling prop keeps target uuids off the visitor view. CSS: single left-rule indent, 320px media query tightening. title: UI: Likes and Reposts tabs + the sidebar Likes strip

Both tabs and the sidebar strip are governed by profiles.likes_visibility and show_likes / show_reposts, stacked on top of each rows indirect visibility.
design:
Likes tab rows: what was liked, when, and where it lives - a collection slug or a source domain plus the author handle. Reposts tab rows: the reposted object rendered as a compact card with its own metadata, plus the repost timestamp.

Every row goes through canSeeIndirect() from task 3.2, which means the query must join the target and its owner. Do not shortcut this by denormalising the target title onto the repost row - task 3.1 deliberately omits those columns for exactly this reason.

Sidebar Likes strip: the count and the thumbnails are BOTH governed by likes_visibility. When likes are private, the whole block is absent for visitors and marked hidden for the owner - never a count with an empty strip, which would leak the number.

title: API: like / unlike, repost / unrepost, reply create-edit-delete
description:
Endpoints for the three conversation actions, following the established handler-plus-thin-route split and the security-definer RPC pattern.

Replies are the only one of the three with a body, so they are the only one needing content validation and an edit path. Likes and reposts are idempotent toggles over a triple.
design:
POST /api/likes { targetType, targetId }        and /api/likes/remove
POST /api/reposts { targetType, targetId }      and /api/reposts/remove
POST /api/replies { targetType, targetId, parentId?, body, visibility }
PATCH /api/replies/[id] { body }   DELETE /api/replies/[id]

Every write validates that the actor CAN SEE the target before creating the row - you cannot like, repost or reply to something you were never allowed to see, and enforcing that at write time stops the row existing at all rather than relying on read-time filtering to hide it.

Reply visibility defaults to the target visibility rather than to public, so replying to a followers-only post does not create a public row exposing that the post exists.

parentId, when present, must reference a reply on the SAME target. Validate this - a reply threaded under a parent on a different object is a data-integrity bug that read-time rendering cannot recover from.

Body validation is pure, in src/lib/reply.ts, alongside a deriveReplySnapshot if any field ever needs excluding.
acceptance_criteria:
- Liking or reposting a target the actor cannot see returns 403 and creates no row.
- Like and repost toggles are idempotent.
- A reply visibility defaults to its target visibility.
- A parentId referencing a reply on a different target is rejected.
- Deleting a reply cascades to its children.
- Handlers unit-tested with a fake store.
close_reason: Conversation write API: src/lib/conversation.ts (parsers + actorCanReachTarget write-time gate), conversationErrors.ts, conversationStore.server.ts (SupabaseConversationStore over the RPCs + resolveTarget/actorFollows), conversationApi.ts (handleLike/Unlike/Repost/Unrepost/CreateReply/UpdateReply/DeleteReply). Routes: /api/likes (POST/DELETE), /api/reposts (POST/DELETE), /api/replies (POST), /api/replies/[replyId] (PATCH/DELETE). CREATE gates on canSee(target); REMOVE never gates. 27 new unit tests (conversation.test.mjs + conversationApi.test.mjs). tsc+lint+build clean, 353 unit + 51 UI green.

title: [Phase 3] Conversation layer: likes, reposts, replies
description:
Three tables that all point at OTHER peoples objects, which makes this phase hard problem indirect visibility rather than schema.

Likes are a lightweight endorsement, governed as a whole list by profiles.likes_visibility rather than per row. Reposts are pure amplification and carry no note. A repost with a note is a REPLY - replies thread, which gives Coeus a comment layer on collections and posts without a separate feature.

Reply nesting renders two levels: a top-level reply and its direct responses. Deeper responses flatten into that second level with a replying-to prefix. Because parent_id exists in the schema, depth is a rendering decision and never a migration.
design:
The correctness centre of this phase is canSeeIndirect(): a repost or like of a collection that later goes private must vanish from the reposter profile. Visibility resolves twice per row - once for the repost, once for the current state of its target.

(target_type, target_id) is polymorphic and Postgres will not enforce it. Deliberate, documented trade: a target_exists trigger on insert, an orphan sweep on the existing daily cron, and canSeeIndirect dropping orphans at read time regardless.
acceptance_criteria:
- All six profile tabs are live.
- Revoking a collection visibility removes it from every profile that reposted or liked it - the INDIRECT case, tested, not just the direct one.
- Replies render two levels with no runaway indentation at 320px.
- likes_visibility governs the whole Likes list and its count together.
close_reason: Phase 3 conversation layer shipped. 7/7 children closed (3.1–3.6 + the 3.7 follow-store bug found during 3.4). All exit criteria met: six profile tabs live; canSeeIndirect() drops an indirect row when its target's visibility is lowered, with a named revocation test at both the pure-function and derive levels; replies render two levels with a 320px-safe single indent; likes_visibility governs the Likes tab, sidebar strip and count together. Gates: 364 unit + 58 component + pgTAP PASS, tsc/lint/build clean. Live-verified against a fresh supabase db reset. Doc docs/profile-page-plan.md §7 marked shipped.

title: Migration: likes, reposts, replies + target_exists trigger
description: The three conversation tables. All three address a target polymorphically as (target_type, target_id), where target_type is a small enum over the things that can be liked, reposted or replied to - initially collection and post.
design:
create type public.target_type as enum ("collection", "post");

likes   (actor_id uuid -> profiles, target_type, target_id uuid, created_at) primary key (actor_id, target_type, target_id)
reposts (id uuid pk, actor_id uuid -> profiles, target_type, target_id uuid, created_at, unique (actor_id, target_type, target_id))
replies (id uuid pk, author_id uuid -> profiles, target_type, target_id uuid, parent_id uuid -> replies(id) on delete cascade, body text check length between 1 and 4000, visibility public.visibility not null default "public", created_at, updated_at)

Indexes: (actor_id, created_at desc) for the profile tabs; (target_type, target_id, created_at desc) for reading a target conversation; replies (parent_id) for the second level.

Reposts carry NO note column - that is the product decision, and leaving the column out is what enforces it.

THE POLYMORPHIC TRADE: (target_type, target_id) cannot be a foreign key. Mitigate with a target_exists trigger on insert that checks the referenced row exists in the table target_type names, plus an orphan sweep added to the existing daily cron at /api/archive/destinations/worker (see vercel.json). Write the trade-off into the migration comment the way the existing migrations document their choices. The alternative - a table per target type - triples the surface for a system with two target types today.

RLS follows posts: permissive select for unlisted/public, owner select over their own rows, writes through security-definer RPCs granted only to service_role.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three tables, the enum, the indexes and the trigger exist.
- Liking the same target twice is idempotent; reposting the same target twice is rejected by the unique constraint.
- Inserting a row whose target does not exist is rejected by the trigger.
- Deleting a reply cascades to its children.
- reposts has no note or body column.
- pgTAP covers the trigger, the unique constraints and the cascade.
close_reason: Migration 20260906170000_conversation_layer.sql: target_type enum; likes/reposts/replies tables + indexes; conversation_target_exists() insert trigger; like/unlike/repost/unrepost/create_reply/update_reply/delete_reply RPCs (service_role only); sweep_conversation_orphans() wired into the daily destinations-worker cron. pgTAP conversation_layer.test.sql (46 assertions) PASS. tsc+lint+build clean, 326 unit + 51 UI green.

title: Discover: a Following view backed by profile_follows
description:
Wire the person graph into the existing Discover surface. Without this, following a person is a number on a page that does nothing - which is worse than not shipping the follow button at all.

Add a Following view to /discover showing collections and posts from people the viewer follows, newest first, filtered through canSee with the viewer as a follower.
design:
src/app/discover/page.tsx currently renders DiscoverApp from SocialApp.tsx, which reads entirely from local archive state and carries a "Discover preview" note saying preview follows do not filter the feed. That note stops being true for this view and should be removed or scoped.

Add a server-side reader alongside the existing listPublic(): listFollowedPeopleContent(viewerId, limit, offset), unioning collection_publications and posts where owner/author is in the viewer follow set and isListable() passes. Order by published_at / created_at desc.

Reuse the range + one-extra-row hasMore idiom from listPublic().

Keep it a distinct VIEW (a segmented control between Everyone and Following), not a ranking change to the existing feed - a filter is legible and testable; a boost is neither at this content volume.

- /discover offers Everyone and Following views.
- The Following view shows only content from followed people.
- A followers-visibility item from a followed person appears; the same item from an unfollowed person does not.
- Unlisted items never appear in either view.

title: Routes: /@handle/followers and /@handle/following
description:
The follower and following lists get their own routes rather than a tab or a modal - real URLs are shareable, paginate naturally, get their own generateMetadata, and keep the profile page query count flat.

Both are server-rendered, paginated, and gated by the show_followers / show_following switches: for a visitor a switched-off list 404s rather than rendering empty, since an empty list and a hidden list should not be distinguishable.
design:
src/app/u/[handle]/followers/page.tsx and .../following/page.tsx, plus a second rewrite rule so the /@ form reaches them:
  { source: "/@:handle/:section", destination: "/u/:handle/:section" }
Confirm this against the mechanism chosen in task 1.1 - if the rewrite went into proxy.ts, extend the same code path there instead.

Gating: use visibleSections() from task 2.8. For a non-owner with the section switched off, call notFound(). For the owner, render with a "hidden from your profile" marker.

Remember that profile_follows.follower_id references auth.users, not profiles: a follower who never completed onboarding has no profile row and must be omitted from the rendered list. The COUNT should also omit them, so the count and the list agree - a count that exceeds the visible rows reads as a bug.

Pagination: cursor on created_at desc using profile_follows_followee_idx. Match the range + one-extra-row hasMore idiom listPublic() already uses in collectionPublicationStore.server.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both routes render at /@handle/followers and /u/handle/followers.
- A switched-off list 404s for a visitor and renders with a hidden marker for the owner.
- Followers without a profile row are omitted from both the list and the count.
- Pagination works past the first page and hasMore is correct at the boundary.
- Each route has its own generateMetadata.
close_reason: followers/following routes + rewrite + ProfileFollowList + pgTAP. Commit 2e01acf.

title: UI: Posts tab + four-value visibility chips in ArchiveApp PublishPanel
description:
Surface the new model in the two places the owner touches it.

On the profile: the Posts tab, rendering published posts through the same view boundary collections use, with the per-viewer filtered count in the sidebar figures.

In the archive: the visibility controls grow from three and two values to four. ArchiveApp.tsx has two of them - the new-collection select at line 394 (private/unlisted/public) and the PublishPanel select at line 79 (unlisted/public). Both become the full four-value set.
design:
Posts tab: a list of post rows - commentary as a pull quote, the source card beneath it, and for the owner an inline visibility chip. Follow the record-row shape the mockup models and the styles already established in src/styles/profile.css from task 1.10.

The sidebar Posts figure is filtered per viewer, per the resolved decision: a visitor sees the public count, a follower sees public plus followers, the owner sees the true total. Compute it from what actually crossed deriveProfileView, never from a raw count - that is what makes it impossible to difference two viewers counts to detect hidden posts.

Visibility chips use the glyph encoding the mockup establishes and which reads without colour: filled circle private, half circle followers, dotted circle unlisted, open circle public. Give each an accessible name, not just a glyph.

In ArchiveApp, the two selects should share one small component rather than being edited twice - a third copy of this list will appear in Phase 3.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Posts tab renders published posts with correct per-viewer filtering.
- The sidebar Posts figure matches the number of rows the viewer can actually see.
- Both ArchiveApp visibility controls offer all four values and persist the choice.
- The visibility control exists as one shared component, used in both places.
- Each visibility option has an accessible name, not only a glyph.
close_reason: Posts tab + ProfilePosts + shared VisibilitySelect/VisibilityGlyph. Commit e45fbd2.

title: UI: ProfileFollowButton + SectionSwitches client islands
description:
Two small client islands.

ProfileFollowButton is FollowButton.tsx with a different endpoint. Keep its structure - including the 401 handling that renders a sign-in message rather than pretending a sign-in flow is one click away - and update the copy now that a sign-in flow does exist.

SectionSwitches renders the five show_* toggles and the likes_visibility control in the owner sidebar, as the mockup models them: pill toggles under a "Show on profile" label, and a separate "Who sees your likes" control.
design:
ProfileFollowButton: rather than fetching the full followed list on mount the way FollowButton does (an O(n) payload to answer one boolean), take the initial following state as a prop from the server component, which already knows it - the profile page resolves the viewer follow relationship anyway for the followers visibility tier (see risk R5). This avoids a second round-trip and a loading flicker.

Consider refactoring FollowButton.tsx the same way afterwards, but do not bundle that into this task.

SectionSwitches: optimistic toggle with rollback on failure. Each toggle is an independent PATCH; a failed one reverts only itself and announces the failure via role=status. Owner-only - never rendered for a visitor.

Both get component tests in the src/components/interaction.test.tsx style.
acceptance_criteria:
- ProfileFollowButton renders the correct initial state at first paint with no fetch on mount.
- A 401 renders a sign-in prompt linking to /signin with next set to the current profile.
- SectionSwitches toggles optimistically and rolls back a failed toggle without affecting the others.
- SectionSwitches is not rendered for a non-owner.
- Component tests pass under npm run test:ui.
close_reason: Two client islands + component tests. ProfileFollowButton: initialFollowing as a server prop (no fetch on mount, no flicker), aria-pressed reflects state, 401 -> sign-in prompt linking /signin?next=%2F%40handle. SectionSwitches: owner-only (returns null for visitor), five role=switch pills + likes-visibility select, each an independent optimistic PATCH with per-field rollback + role=status announcement on failure. Styles in profile.css. 6 new tests in interaction.test.tsx; test:ui 28 green, full suite 336 green, tsc + eslint clean. NOT yet wired into ProfileView — see follow-up.

title: AccountMenu: point Edit profile at /@handle and add View profile
description:
The change that makes the page discoverable to its own owner. AccountMenu.tsx currently sends "Edit profile" to /welcome?next=<pathname> - the onboarding form - which is the right destination only while no profile page exists.

Point it at the profile instead. Add a "View profile" item, and keep "Finish your profile" pointing at /welcome for the needs-profile state, where there is no handle to route to yet.
design:
In src/components/AccountMenu.tsx the editHref constant becomes conditional on profile being present:
- profile present: View profile and Edit profile both route to /@<profile.handle> (the editor opens in place there, so they can be one item or two - two reads better in the menu).
- profile absent (status needs-profile): keep the single "Finish your profile" item pointing at /welcome?next=<pathname>.

Nothing else in the menu changes. ProfileGate.tsx keeps redirecting needs-profile accounts to /welcome; that flow is untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- A signed-in account with a profile sees View profile and Edit profile, both routing to /@handle.
- A signed-in account without a profile still sees Finish your profile routing to /welcome.
- Signed-out state is unchanged.
- No dead link to /welcome remains for an onboarded account.
close_reason: AccountMenu: with a profile, 'View profile' -> /@handle and 'Edit profile' -> /@handle?edit=1 (both route to /@handle; the editor opens in place). Without a profile, 'Finish your profile' -> /welcome unchanged. Signed-out unchanged. No /welcome dead link for an onboarded account. interaction.test.tsx updated: asserts both items present and their router.push targets.

title: UI: ProfileEditor client island + component test
description:
The one client island in Phase 1. Lets the owner edit bio, location, external links and cover/avatar in place on their own profile, rather than being sent back to /welcome.

Follow the inline-editor pattern ArchiveApp.tsx already uses - a details element containing the form, opened in place - rather than inventing a modal or a separate settings route. Consistency with the existing editing idiom matters more than novelty here.

Saves go to PUT /api/account/profile for text and POST /api/account/profile/media for images (task 1.9). Handle the 422 per-field error shape the API already returns, surfacing each message next to its field.
design:
Mounted only when isOwner. Receives the current values as props from the server component so it renders correct at first paint with no loading flash.

Link editing: up to five rows of label + url, add and remove, matching the five-entry cap the database check enforces in task 1.2. Validate client-side with validateProfileLinks() from task 1.7 - the same function the API uses - so the client and server can never disagree about what is valid.

Cover control: a two-way choice between the generated cover and an uploaded photo, exactly as the mockup models it. Choosing "generated" clears cover_url to null rather than uploading anything.

Test in src/components/interaction.test.tsx style (jsdom + @testing-library/react, dynamic imports after the JSDOM globals are assigned - follow the existing file header exactly). Cover: a successful save, a 422 rendering per-field errors, and the link count cap.
acceptance_criteria:
- The editor renders with current values at first paint, with no loading state.
- A successful save updates the page without a full reload.
- A 422 response renders each field error beside its field.
- Adding a sixth link is prevented client-side.
- Choosing the generated cover clears cover_url.
- Component test passes under npm run test:ui.
close_reason: src/components/ProfileEditor.tsx: inline <details> editor (ProfileEditorMount supplies router.refresh as onSaved so ProfileEditor itself stays testable without next/navigation). Edits bio/location/links/avatar/cover; link rows capped at 5 client-side via the shared validateProfileLinks(); 'Generated' cover choice sends coverUrl:null; 422 -> per-field errors beside each field; images -> POST media then included in the PUT. Mounted only for isOwner; ?edit=1 opens it. 5 tests in profileEditor.test.tsx (jsdom, interaction.test.tsx header) pass.

title: lib/profileMedia.ts: deterministic generative cover + avatar initials
description:
A profile with no uploaded cover must still look deliberate. Generate one from the handle: a monospace character field, seeded so the same handle always produces the same cover, on this render and on every future one.

Port the algorithm proven in the mockup artifact: an FNV-1a hash of the handle seeding a mulberry32 PRNG, filling a grid from the ramp of increasing-density characters with a diagonal gradient bias. Also export avatarInitials(displayName) for the square avatar fallback.

Determinism is the whole point and it is also what makes this trivially testable - the test is a fixture comparison, not a visual check.
design:
Exports:
  coverSeed(handle: string): number            // FNV-1a, returns an unsigned 32-bit value
  generativeCover(handle, cols, rows): string  // newline-joined rows from the ramp
  avatarInitials(displayName: string): string  // one or two uppercase letters

Pure, no DOM, no randomness beyond the seeded PRNG. Rendered server-side into the banner as a pre element with aria-hidden, so it costs no client JavaScript.

Ramp and default dimensions come from the mockup: " .-:+=*%#" at roughly 170 by 22 for a desktop banner. The component decides dimensions; the lib only fills a grid it is given.

Tests in src/lib/profileMedia.test.mjs: same handle gives byte-identical output twice; two different handles give different output; output dimensions match the requested cols and rows exactly; avatarInitials handles one word, two words, extra whitespace and non-Latin input without throwing.
acceptance_criteria:
- generativeCover is byte-identical across repeated calls with the same handle.
- Output row count and row length match the requested dimensions exactly.
- Two different handles produce different covers.
- avatarInitials never throws and never returns more than two characters.
- No DOM or crypto dependency; runs under node --test.
close_reason: src/lib/profileMedia.ts: coverSeed (FNV-1a uint32), generativeCover (mulberry32 over the ' .-:+=*%#' ramp with a diagonal gradient bias), avatarInitials. Deterministic, no DOM/crypto. 7 tests: byte-identical repeats, exact requested dimensions, ramp-only output, initials <=2 chars incl. non-Latin. Renders in the live page's aria-hidden <pre>.

title: Migration: profile-media storage bucket + owner-prefixed write policy
description:
Create a PUBLIC Supabase Storage bucket for avatars and covers. The project already runs a private archive-snapshots bucket (supabase/migrations/20260904120000_synced_archives.sql), so this reuses a system already in the stack rather than introducing Vercel Blob as a second storage vendor and a second credential.

A public bucket with user-controlled paths is a general-purpose file host if left open, so the write policy restricts each account to its own path prefix and the upload route (task 1.9) additionally caps MIME type and size. Both layers, not either.
design:
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public) values ("profile-media", "profile-media", true);

Policies on storage.objects, scoped to bucket_id = "profile-media":
- select: allow to public (the bucket is public by design - these images render for signed-out visitors).
- insert / update / delete: to authenticated, with (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select auth.uid())::text, so an account can only write under its own uid prefix.

Path convention: <uid>/avatar-<random>.<ext> and <uid>/cover-<random>.<ext>. A random component in the filename avoids CDN cache staleness when an image is replaced, which matters because the bucket is public and therefore cacheable.

Follow the existing storage policy in 20260904120000_synced_archives.sql for the exact idiom used in this project.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bucket exists and is public.
- An authenticated account can write under its own uid prefix and cannot write under another uid prefix.
- An anonymous request can read an object but cannot write one.
- pgTAP covers the cross-account write rejection.
notes: Risk R3 in docs/profile-page-plan.md. Decision: Supabase Storage over Vercel Blob, overriding the original mockup spec.
close_reason: Same migration creates public profile-media bucket + storage.objects policies: public select; insert/update/delete restricted to (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text. pgTAP: bucket is public, own-prefix write ok, cross-account write 42501, anon read ok, anon write 42501 — all pass.
