description: Run the full publish -> public page -> RSS -> follow -> discover flow against a running local Supabase stack (supabase start / db reset) the way 6j1.5 validated sync. Confirm anon/unauthenticated reads only see published public/unlisted material, owner-only writes are enforced, and pgTAP RLS tests pass.
design: Check df -h before assuming a Docker/disk problem, per prior session note about tight local disk space.
acceptance_criteria: npm run test:db passes for the new tables' RLS policies; a live smoke test confirms an unauthenticated client can read a published collection and its RSS feed but not private archive data.
notes: Disk was at 8.3GB free (97% used, tighter than the ~16GB the prior session flagged) -- pruned 12.66GB of reclaimable/unused Docker images (0 active containers, 0 active images at the time) with explicit user approval before starting Supabase, per the session's disk-tightness note. supabase start -> supabase db reset applied all four migrations cleanly, including this epic's two new ones (20260904140000_collection_publications.sql, 20260904150000_collection_follows.sql) with zero errors -- confirms the schema/RLS/RPC SQL is syntactically and semantically valid, not just plausible-looking. New supabase/tests/collection_publications.test.sql (21 pgTAP tests, all passing alongside the existing 12 in archive_sync.test.sql = 33/33) covers: publish_collection creates a row+items, republish keeps the original slug even when a different one is requested and replaces items wholesale, unpublish_collection sets unpublished_at, RLS lets a non-owner read a live public/unlisted publication but not an unpublished one (while the owner still can), the collection_follows RLS policy allows self-follow/self-unfollow but rejects following on someone else's behalf (42501), and authenticated clients cannot call publish_collection/unpublish_collection directly (service-role only, 42501). Additionally ran a live smoke test (temporary script, deleted after -- not committed) exercising the actual production SupabaseCollectionPublicationStore class end-to-end against the live stack with two real auth.admin.createUser() accounts: publish -> republish (slug stability, visibility update) -> getBySlug -> list (owner's own) -> listPublic (discovery, correct itemCount) -> follow -> listFollowed -> unfollow -> unpublish (drops out of both getBySlug and listPublic). Explicitly asserted no ArchiveItem.note field appears on any published item. All passed. npm test 102/102, tsc, lint clean throughout. Stopped the Supabase stack afterward (disk pressure); .env.local with local dev keys was left in place (gitignored) for future sessions' convenience. bareaga_web-5bv (parent epic) is now fully validated end-to-end and ready to close.
close_reason: Live-validated against a real local Supabase stack: all four migrations (including the epic's two new ones) applied cleanly via db reset; 33/33 pgTAP tests pass (21 new, covering publish/republish/unpublish RPCs and RLS for collection_publications/collection_publication_items/collection_follows); a live smoke test of the actual production store class confirmed the full publish->discover->follow->unpublish lifecycle and that no private archive field leaks onto a published item.

title: Add follows and public collection discovery
description: Authenticated follow/unfollow of a published collection (collection_follows table, RLS scoped to follower_id = auth.uid()), and a discovery listing surface for public (not unlisted) collections with pagination, wired for a later connection to Explore.
design: Unlisted collections stay reachable only via direct slug link and are excluded from discovery listing at the query level.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-in user can follow and unfollow a public collection; a discovery page lists public collections without exposing unlisted or private ones; follow state persists across devices via the synced auth session.
notes: supabase/migrations/20260904150000_collection_follows.sql: collection_follows(publication_id, follower_id) with a single 'for all' RLS policy -- USING scopes select/update/delete to follower_id = auth.uid(), WITH CHECK additionally requires the target publication be live (unpublished_at is null, visibility in public/unlisted) so a follow can't be created against a withdrawn/private row. No RPC needed (unlike publish/unpublish): a follow only ever references a publication row, so authenticated users manage their own rows directly under RLS, same pattern as the archives table's owner-insert policy. Store: SupabaseCollectionPublicationStore gained PublicCollectionReader.listPublic() (visibility='public' only, per the design note -- unlisted stays link-only and never appears in discovery; offset/limit pagination fetches one extra row to compute hasMore, then a separate items count query grouped in JS rather than relying on untested PostgREST embedded-relationship count syntax) and CollectionFollowStore (follow/unfollow/listFollowed, preserving most-recently-followed order). API: /api/collections/discover (unauthenticated, public cache headers), /follow, /unfollow, /followed (authenticated). UI: new /c (discovery index, offset-paginated) and a FollowButton client component wired into /c/[slug] -- note there is no sign-in UI anywhere in this codebase yet (only signout/delete assume an existing session), so FollowButton surfaces the 401 as 'sign in to your Bareaga account' text rather than linking a sign-in flow that doesn't exist. ArchiveApp's Publish panel now links to /c. Did not touch /discover (DiscoverApp/SocialApp) or PrimaryNav -- the bead explicitly frames connecting this to Explore as later work, not part of 5bv. Verification: npm test (102/102), tsc --noEmit, lint, build all clean, all new routes present in the build's route table. NOT verified: live Supabase (RLS policy execution, actual follow persistence) -- same constraint as 5bv.1-5bv.3, deferred to 5bv.5.
close_reason: Follows (collection_follows table + RLS) and a public-collection discovery listing (/c index + /api/collections/discover, scoped to visibility=public only) are implemented, with follow/unfollow wired into a new FollowButton on /c/[slug]. 102/102 tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean. Live Supabase verification deferred to 5bv.5, the last remaining subtask of bareaga_web-5bv.

title: Add public collection pages and RSS output
description: Unauthenticated, stable public URL (e.g. /c/[slug]) rendering a published collection's items, curator notes, and attribution using either RLS-scoped public reads or an admin client with explicit visibility filtering. Add an RSS 2.0 feed endpoint per published collection for update tracking.
design: No client-side direct PostgREST access from the browser; server-rendered page + route handler use the admin client with explicit visibility filtering, matching the rest of the codebase's server API pattern. RLS stays as defense-in-depth.
acceptance_criteria: A public/unlisted collection is viewable at its stable URL by an unauthenticated visitor; private archive material is never exposed; an RSS feed is available and validates against the collection's published items.
notes: src/lib/collectionPublicationStore.server.ts: SupabaseCollectionPublicationStore now also implements PublicCollectionReader.getBySlug(slug) -- an unauthenticated read using the admin client with EXPLICIT visibility/unpublished filtering (not relying on the collection_publications RLS policy as the enforcement point, since the admin client bypasses RLS entirely; RLS stays defense-in-depth for a hypothetical future direct client read), per the design note on the bead. src/lib/collectionPublicationRss.ts: dependency-free RSS 2.0 generator (renderCollectionRss) with XML escaping and a self-referencing atom:link; deliberately omits per-item pubDate since derivePublicationSnapshot() (5bv.1) never carries the private savedAt an item pubDate would need -- 5 unit tests cover escaping, ordering by position, and structure. src/app/c/[slug]/page.tsx: unauthenticated server-rendered public collection page (React cache() dedupes the generateMetadata + page reads of the same slug within one request); src/app/c/[slug]/rss.xml/route.ts: the feed endpoint. Both intentionally do NOT catch-and-404 on a thrown error from the store -- only a genuine null (not found/unpublished/private) becomes a 404; a real backend error (e.g. Supabase outage) is left to fall through to Next's default error handling, so a misconfigured deployment surfaces as a 500 rather than silently reading as 'every collection link is broken.' New src/styles/public-collection.css registered in globals.css, reusing existing design tokens (no new page-level CSS system). Verification: npm test (99/99), tsc --noEmit, lint, and build all clean, including the new dynamic routes appearing in the build's route table. NOT verified: an actual browser hit against a live page -- this repo has no .env.local and the local Supabase stack is stopped, so createAdminSupabaseClient() would throw immediately regardless of route code; a real end-to-end check needs the live stack from 5bv.5 (which needs approval to start).
close_reason: Public /c/[slug] page and /c/[slug]/rss.xml feed implemented on top of the 5bv.1/5bv.2 contract and store, with explicit (non-RLS-reliant) visibility filtering for the unauthenticated admin-client read path. 99/99 tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean. Live browser/Supabase verification deferred to 5bv.5 (no .env.local or running local stack in this environment).

title: Define collection publication architecture and contract
description: Design how a private, JSON-embedded archive collection becomes a stable, publicly-readable object without exposing private archive material. Specify normalized Postgres tables (collection_publications, collection_publication_items, collection_follows) separate from the private archives/archive_revisions tables, RLS policies for public/unlisted reads and service-role-only writes, slug generation/uniqueness, and a TS domain module that derives a public-safe publication snapshot (title, description, curator note, attribution, per-item title/url/source/excerpt/curator comment) from a private ArchiveCollection + its items, explicitly excluding private fields (personal note, tags, state, starred, topic).
design: Mirror the 6j1.1 pattern: schema + RLS as SQL migration, runtime-validated TS contract, deterministic unit tests before any API/UI work.
acceptance_criteria: Executable Postgres migration with RLS/RPC exists; a TS module can derive a validated public-safe publication payload from private archive data with unit tests covering slug uniqueness and field exclusion; design documented in bead notes/design.
notes: Schema: supabase/migrations/20260904140000_collection_publications.sql adds collection_publications + collection_publication_items, normalized and separate from archives/archive_revisions (which stay owner-only). RLS: anon+authenticated may SELECT any row where unpublished_at is null and visibility in (public,unlisted); owners can additionally SELECT their own drafts/unpublished rows via archives.owner_id join. All writes go through two SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (service_role only, revoked from anon/authenticated), mirroring initialize_archive/commit_archive_sync: publish_collection() (upsert keyed on (archive_id, collection_local_id); slug is assigned once and never changes on republish; items are replaced wholesale each publish) and unpublish_collection() (soft-delete via unpublished_at). Discovery (public vs unlisted) is a query-level filter on top of RLS, not a separate policy. TS contract: src/lib/collectionPublication.ts defines CollectionPublicationSnapshot/Item types, proposeSlug/slugWithSuffix (retry-on-collision is the caller's job in 5bv.2), derivePublicationSnapshot(collection, items, options) which explicitly excludes item.note/tags/state/starred/topic/savedAt/articleId (per-item curatorComment is only ever supplied explicitly, never defaulted from the private note), and parsePublicationSnapshot() for runtime validation of the wire payload, mirroring archiveSync.ts's parse* pattern. 12 unit tests in collectionPublication.test.mjs cover slug validity, item ordering/filtering, the private-field exclusion guarantee, and payload validation edge cases. npm test (89/89), npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, and npm run build all pass. Migration was NOT applied against a live Supabase instance this session (stack was stopped; starting/resetting it needs explicit approval per session instructions) — reviewed carefully against the syntax/RLS conventions already proven working in 20260904120000_synced_archives.sql. Live RLS verification is 5bv.5's job; 5bv.2 can now build the authenticated publish/unpublish/update API routes and store on top of this contract.
close_reason: Publication schema, RLS, service-role RPCs, and a runtime-validated TS domain contract are implemented and unit-tested (89/89 tests, tsc, lint, build all clean). Live Supabase RLS verification deferred to 5bv.5 pending approval to start the local stack.

title: Maximum update depth exceeded loop in Reader slash-command registration
description: During dcu.4 (add-source-by-URL UI) manual testing, dev logging showed a repeated 'Maximum update depth exceeded' React warning. Root cause: the effect in NewsApp.tsx that registers Reader commands into ChromeProvider's readerSlash state (via setReaderSlash) previously returned a cleanup that cleared readerSlash to null on every dependency-array change, not just on unmount. Since currentSources (from useFeedQuery) and other deps change frequently, this null-then-set cycle on every re-run drove repeated context updates and looped the render tree.
design: Fix already present in the current (uncommitted) working tree at src/components/NewsApp.tsx:139-179: (1) the registration effect now bails out via a functional setReaderSlash update that returns the previous object unchanged when topic/search/sources/busy are unchanged, avoiding redundant state updates; (2) the null-clearing cleanup was moved to its own effect with dependency array [setReaderSlash] only (a stable setState setter), so it fires solely on unmount instead of on every dependency change. This is the standard fix for this class of React loop.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise AddSourceForm and Reader topic/search/refresh flows in a real browser with devtools open; confirm no 'Maximum update depth exceeded' warning appears in the console across topic switches, search typing, and refresh.
notes: Dev server terminal logs (2026-09-04) show clean, successful /archive, /, and /api/feeds requests with no crash/error during a session that exercised these flows — consistent with the fix holding, though terminal HTTP logs do not capture browser-console React warnings, so this is not itself conclusive. Filing so dcu.4 does not close with this regression untracked.
close_reason: Live-verified fixed in browser (2026-09-04): loaded /, exercised topic switching, search typing, force refresh; loaded /discover, added a live Substack source (heathercoxrichardson.substack.com) via AddSourceForm, confirmed it rendered in Reader alongside catalog sources (22/23 sources, 185 stories), then removed it. Read browser console via read_console_messages with an unfiltered pattern across the whole sequence -- only [HMR] connected logs appeared, zero React warnings/errors, no 'Maximum update depth exceeded'. Confirms the code fix documented at NewsApp.tsx:139-179 (bailout comparison + unmount-only cleanup effect) holds under the exact flows that originally surfaced the bug.

title: Feed URL discovery: Substack convention + HTML autodiscovery
description: Users will paste a publication URL (e.g. a Substack homepage or a blog's homepage), not a raw feed URL. Resolve a pasted URL to an actual RSS/Atom feed: try the Substack '/feed' convention first, then fall back to fetching the page HTML and parsing <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml|application/atom+xml> autodiscovery tags (covers WordPress, Ghost, and most static-site blogs). If a feed URL is pasted directly, use it as-is. Must build on the SSRF-safe fetch from the sibling hardening task.
design: Two-tier resolution: (1) known-convention guess (Substack /feed) tried first since it avoids an extra HTML fetch, (2) generic autodiscovery via HTML <link> tag as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Pasting a Substack publication URL, a WordPress/Ghost blog homepage, or a direct feed URL all resolve to a working feed; an unresolvable URL produces a clear error rather than a silent failure.
close_reason: Implemented direct-feed passthrough, native Substack /feed resolution, HTML RSS/Atom autodiscovery, SSRF-safe candidate fetching, clear failures, and regression coverage; verified against a live Substack homepage.

title: Add live Obsidian and Notion sync adapters

notes: Architecture decided 2026-09-04: Obsidian via a GitHub git-repo bridge (server pushes Markdown via Contents/Tree API using a user PAT; user syncs the repo into their vault with any Obsidian git plugin). Push is automatic after each /api/archive/sync commit (via after()) plus a Vercel Cron catch-up/retry worker, driven off archiveSync.ts's existing entityVersions revision tracking rather than a second diff pass. Secrets encrypted in Node (AES-256-GCM) at rest, never in Postgres. Full design in /Users/dylanchidambaram/.claude/plans/sparkling-kindling-wigderson.md. Sequenced as 2u2.1 (schema/contracts) -> 2u2.2 (Obsidian/GitHub, first vertical slice) and 2u2.3 (Notion OAuth) in parallel -> 2u2.4 (UI) -> 2u2.5 (live suite), mirroring 6j1's phasing.
close_reason: All children (2u2.1-2u2.5) complete. Live Obsidian/GitHub + Notion OAuth adapters, destinations store/API, delivery worker, DestinationsPanel UI, and cron catch-up all shipped and verified against real GitHub + real Notion. title: isUnsafeIp misses IPv6 transition ranges: NAT64 / 6to4 / Teredo (F-30)
description: ipv6IsUnsafe (safeOutboundFetch.server.ts) covers ::, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, ff00::/8, 2001:db8::/32, and decodes IPv4-mapped/compatible. It does NOT reject 64:ff9b::/96 + 64:ff9b:1::/48 (NAT64, RFC 6052/8215), 2002::/16 (6to4, RFC 3056), or 2001::/32 (Teredo, RFC 4380) — all embed an IPv4 that could be a private/loopback address on a host that routes the transition mechanism. Vercel Node runtime unlikely to route these today; base-image change could open it. Existing 'reject if ANY resolved address is unsafe' logic blunts the classic one-good-one-bad DNS trick.
design: In ipv6IsUnsafe: detect 64:ff9b::/96 (+64:ff9b:1::/48), 2002::/16, 2001::/32; extract the embedded IPv4 (groups[6..7] for NAT64, groups[1..2] for 6to4, groups[2..3] for Teredo) and run ipv4IsUnsafe on it.
acceptance_criteria: safeOutboundFetch.server.test.mjs (NEW — module has no dedicated test; see findings §5) with fixtures for 64:ff9b::7f00:1, 2002:7f00:1::, 2001:0:xxxx (loopback-embedding), plus a few public IPv6 addresses that must stay allowed. Drop the server-only guard per server-only-vs-node-test memory convention with a comment.
close_reason: Fixed: ipv6IsUnsafe now handles NAT64 64:ff9b::/96 (embedded IPv4 -> ipv4IsUnsafe), rejects the 64:ff9b:1::/48 local-use prefix wholesale, and decodes the embedded IPv4 of 2002::/16 (6to4) and 2001::/32 (Teredo, both server + one's-complement client fields). New safeOutboundFetch.server.test.mjs — 14 cases, closes the findings §5 no-test gap for this module. 494 unit green; tsc + eslint clean.

description:
Phase 3 of the profile epic creates the four events worth notifying on - a new follower, a like, a reply, a repost - and then deliberately stops. This epic is filed so the work is visible and blocked, not started.

Doing it properly needs its own table, a read/unread model, a header surface, digest batching to avoid notifying on every single event, and probably email - which this project has no sender for. That is an epic, and folding it into the profile work would swallow the profile work.
design:
Deliberately unplanned. Plan it when Phase 3 closes and there is real event volume to design against - notification design is mostly a batching and threshold problem, and both are unanswerable without data.

Prerequisite not yet in the stack: an email sender. Evaluate whether in-app only is sufficient for a first version before adding one.
acceptance_criteria: - Not applicable until planned. This issue is a placeholder; planning it produces its own tree.
notes: Filed 2026-09-06 during profile-page planning. Blocked on the Phase 3 sub-epic.

title: Overview: revisit the interleave decision with real data
description:
The resolved decision is that Overview shows first-party content only - own collections and own posts, interleaved by recency - with reposts and replies confined to their own tabs.

Once Phase 3 has shipped and there is real content on real profiles, revisit it. If Overview reads thin on an active account, widen it to interleave reposts and replies. If it reads busy, leave it.

This task exists so the decision gets re-examined against evidence rather than either being silently changed or silently forgotten.
design:
If widened, Overview becomes a four-source union with per-row canSeeIndirect checks, which makes it the most expensive query on the page - so the widening should come with a look at whether it needs a materialised feed rather than a live union.

Do not widen speculatively. Close this as no-change if the first-party feed reads well.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded in this issue, with the reason and what was observed.
- Either Overview is widened with the query cost measured, or the issue is closed as no-change with the observation noted.
close_reason: No change. Overview stays first-party-only (own collections + own posts by recency); reposts and replies now live in their own tabs (3.4/3.5). No production profile data yet to argue for widening, and the plan is explicit: do not widen speculatively. Revisit if an active account's Overview reads thin — widening = a four-source canSeeIndirect union that would want a materialised feed, per this issue's design note.

title: Add archiveRecoveryApi handler test coverage
description: archiveRecoveryApi.ts (export/revisions/restore/capture/download/account-delete handlers from bareaga_web-6j1.4) has zero test coverage, unlike archiveApi.ts (archiveApi.test.mjs) and collectionPublicationApi.ts (collectionPublicationApi.test.mjs added in bareaga_web-5bv). Add archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs with a fake in-memory ArchiveRecoveryStore, mirroring the established pattern. Separately, desugar SupabaseArchiveRecoveryStore's parameter-property constructor to match archiveSyncStore.server.ts's convention, for consistency (not currently a live blocker since archiveRecoveryApi.ts checks errors by message string rather than instanceof, so no value import from the server-only-guarded file is needed for handler tests).
acceptance_criteria: archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs exists and passes, covering auth checks and the success/error status-code paths for each handler; npm test, tsc --noEmit, lint, and build remain clean.
notes: archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs added, 6 tests, all passing, no blocker hit: unlike collectionPublicationApi.ts, archiveRecoveryApi.ts maps store errors by message string comparison (e.g. cause.message === 'Revision not found') rather than instanceof a custom Error class, so the fake MemoryArchiveRecoveryStore never needed a value import from the server-only-guarded archiveRecoveryStore.server.ts -- only ArchiveRecoveryStore's type shape matters, which a plain JS fake object satisfies structurally without any import at all. Also desugared SupabaseArchiveRecoveryStore's parameter-property constructor to match archiveSyncStore.server.ts's convention, for consistency (this specific fix wasn't required for the new test to pass, but removes the same latent trap for any future test that does need a value import from that file). 121/121 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.
close_reason: Added archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs (6 tests covering all six handlers' auth/validation/status-code paths) and desugared SupabaseArchiveRecoveryStore's constructor for consistency with archiveSyncStore.server.ts. 121/121 tests, tsc, lint, build all clean.

title: Add www.coeuscoeus.com redirect to the apex
description: www.coeuscoeus.com currently returns nothing (CNAME -> cname.vercel-dns.com exists but the domain is not attached in Vercel). Add www.coeuscoeus.com in Vercel coeus project Settings -> Domains as a redirect to https://coeuscoeus.com so the www host works and gets an SSL cert.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-09: http://www.coeuscoeus.com returns Vercel's default 308 -> https://www.coeuscoeus.com/, but https fails (no cert: 'no alternative certificate subject name matches www.coeuscoeus.com') because the host is not attached to the project. www CNAME -> cname.vercel-dns.com is already in place. No code fix possible — vercel.json cannot attach a domain. MANUAL STEP (dashboard or CLI): Vercel > project 'coeus' > Settings > Domains > Add 'www.coeuscoeus.com' > choose 'Redirect to coeuscoeus.com' (308). CLI equivalent: 'vercel domains add www.coeuscoeus.com' then set the redirect in the dashboard, or 'vercel project ... '. Cert issues automatically once attached. Then re-verify: curl -I https://www.coeuscoeus.com should 308 to https://coeuscoeus.com/.
